Article Title: Russia-US diesel deal delivers results? Lavrov claims prices have already fallen
Article Text:
Russia hails diesel deal with US (representative image)

US-bound shipments face uncertainty

Lavrov raises Ukraine strikes on Russian energy infrastructure

Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov has said an agreement allowing Russia to resume diesel exports to the United States and global markets is already being implemented and has helped bring prices down.In an article published in Moscow daily Kommersant on Tuesday, Lavrov said the arrangement was an important contribution to energy security. He also argued that Russia did not use its economy to score political points against countries it considered adversaries or competitors.Also Read| Iran war, cost of living drag Trump’s approval rating near career low: Survey “Since 2022, we have supplied Europe with energy resources worth $320 billion,” Lavrov wrote.“An important contribution to energy security was the agreement between the Russian and US leaders to suspend restrictions on the export of Russian diesel. We have already started implementing it, which immediately brought prices down.”US President Donald Trump announced the deal on October 9. Under the arrangement, Russia agreed to make 300,000 metric tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, of diesel available immediately to the US and global markets, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and a further 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.The Trump administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel to facilitate the exports.The move came as the US president sought to bring down fuel prices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which his Republican Party lost.Lavrov did not provide figures to support his claim that the agreement had lowered diesel prices.US diesel futures have fallen about 11% since the deal was announced, according to Reuters.However, diesel prices at US pumps were at a record high last week when Americans voted, according to price tracker GasBuddy.The arrangement has also faced uncertainty over whether Russian fuel would reach the US.Two sanctioned tankers that had initially declared destinations on the US East Coast changed course, while a third vessel travelling across the North Atlantic changed its destination from New York to “for orders”, according to news agency AP.The report said the proposed imports had yet to result in a confirmed US delivery. Analysts also questioned whether the shipments would reach American ports, citing regulatory and sanctions-related concerns.New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill had advised port and terminal operators in the state to reject Russian fuel shipments, warning of possible legal consequences. A bipartisan group of US senators also urged Trump to abandon the arrangement, arguing that it could provide financial support to Moscow.The US Treasury Department, however, maintained that its temporary authorisation for Russian diesel transactions was consistent with previous actions and “in compliance with all applicable laws”.The exemption was issued for the sale, delivery, unloading and import of Russian diesel until April 7.Separately, Russian deputy foreign minister Alexander Pankin said on Monday that the diesel arrangement could provide an opportunity for the gradual restoration of business and other ties between Moscow and Washington.He told the TASS state news agency that the deal could “serve as a foundation for the gradual restoration of business and other ties between our countries”.In his Kommersant article, Lavrov said Russia was working to stabilise global energy markets and ensure energy security, as well as the balanced and sustainable development of countries and regions.He also accused Ukraine of ignoring Trump's calls to stop attacks on Russian energy infrastructure.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last week that Kyiv's forces were continuing their strikes.Russian media have reported that fuel shortages have returned in at least half a dozen Russian regions following Ukrainian attacks on at least eight major oil refineries over the past two weeks.
Article Summary: Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov hails diesel deal with US. Deal allows Russia to resume diesel exports to the United States and global markets. US President Donald Trump announced the deal on October 9. The arrangement has faced uncertainty over whether Russian fuel would reach the US.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Crude edges lower as Donald Trump signals pause in military action against Iran
Article Text:
Crude oil eases (representative image)

Trump signals pause in strikes, but Hormuz blockade to continue

Opec output rises, Russia-Ukraine talks in focus

Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday, extending the previous session's losses, after US President Donald Trump said military action against Iran was not necessary “at this point”. His remarks eased concerns over prolonged disruptions to oil supplies from the Middle East.Brent crude futures fell 24 cents, or 0.23%, to $92.33 a barrel by 0102 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 35 cents, or 0.40%, to $86.50 a barrel.Brent had settled 5.85% lower in the previous session after falling to its lowest level since August 31.Trump said on Monday that he planned to hold off on fresh military strikes against Iran for the time being, following appeals from countries in the region. These included an appeal from Qatar's prime minister during talks at the White House.In an interview with Reuters and a subsequent appearance in the White House briefing room, Trump said the US would maintain its naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now.“The market continues to prioritise President Trump's more conciliatory tone toward Iran since the midterms,” said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.He added that attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz were continuing but had not escalated enough to bring a fresh risk premium into the market.However, senior US and Gulf officials have expressed doubts about the possibility of an imminent peace deal between Washington and Tehran.Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei rejected reports of negotiations, saying the US should “stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks”.He added that it was “time to surrender to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out”.On the supply side, oil production by the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (Opec) increased in October, according to a Reuters survey. The rise was led by higher output in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq, despite continued constraints on exports.Elsewhere, Russian and Ukrainian officials were scheduled to meet on Tuesday for two days of US-brokered talks. The meeting would be their first since February.Trump had suggested last week that a broader peace agreement could be possible in the 4.5-year-old Russia-Ukraine war and could also incorporate Europe's security.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 0.23%, to $92.33 a barrel by 0102 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 35 cents, to $86.50 a barrel. Trump said he planned to hold off on fresh military strikes against Iran for the time being.

Article Title: Stock market holiday today: Are NSE, BSE open or closed on November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada? Check details
Article Text:
Stock market open or closed on Nov 10?

Are NSE and BSE closed?

The festive season has brought changes to the regular trading schedule, with Indian stock exchanges observing holidays around Diwali. After a special Muhurat Trading session on Sunday and a regular trading session on Monday, investors may be looking to resume trading on Tuesday, November 10.According to the 2026 holiday calendar of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), will remain closed on account of Diwali-Balipratipada. The holiday applies to the equity, equity derivatives and securities lending and borrowing (SLB) segments, among other market segments.Sensex and Nifty ended higher on Monday, recovering after marginally slipping in the special Muhurat trading session on Sunday. The Sensex rose 107.25 points, or 0.13 per cent, to 81,106.65, while the Nifty gained 58.25 points, or 0.23 per cent, to reclaim the 25,000 mark at 25,044.65. Buying in banking and financial stocks, along with a decline in crude oil prices, supported the benchmarks, although losses in IT and metal shares capped gains. Brent crude fell 1.04 per cent to $97.46 per barrel.Also read: Are banks open or closed on November 10, 2026? Check state-wise list Yes. Both the NSE and BSE will remain closed on Tuesday, November 10, for Diwali-Balipratipada.Trading will remain suspended across the equity, equity derivatives and SLB segments. The capital market, derivatives market, electronic gold receipts (EGR) and debt market will also remain closed.The exchanges will resume normal trading on Wednesday, November 11, with the regular equity market session scheduled from 9:15 am to 3:30 pm.Meanwhile, the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) will remain closed during the morning session, from 9 am to 5 pm. However, trading will resume in the evening session from 5 pm to 11:30 pm.The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX), meanwhile, will remain closed for the entire day.The exchanges have declared November 10 a trading holiday on account of Diwali-Balipratipada, also known as Bali Pratipada. The festival is observed on the day after Diwali and marks the annual return of King Mahabali to his kingdom, according to Hindu mythology.The holiday follows the special Muhurat Trading session held on Sunday, November 8, to mark the beginning of Samvat 2083, the Hindu financial year. The exchanges subsequently conducted a regular trading session on Monday, November 9.After the November 10 closure, the next scheduled trading holiday for the NSE and BSE is November 24, Tuesday, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev.The exchanges will also remain closed on December 25 for Christmas, according to their 2026 holiday calendars, apart from the regular weekend holidays.
Article Summary: NSE and BSE will remain closed on Tuesday, November 10, for Diwali- Balipratipada. The holiday applies to the equity, equity derivatives and securities lending and borrowing (SLB) segments. The capital market, derivatives market, electronic gold receipts (EGR) and debt market will also remain closed.

Article Title: Will probe into Nvidia's Jensen Huang indirectly benefit Indian stock markets?
Article Text:
Nvidia announced the probe on Sunday, following Huang's admission that he had been intimate with a business executive. (Image for representative purpose only)

What has happened

Does it impact India?

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Nvidia, one of the most valuable listed companies in the world, is in the eye of the storm with the company launching an investigation into reports that its chief executive, Jensen Huang, had been the “target of a foreign intelligence effort. ” Nvidia shares dropped 8% at the start of trading on Monday.Nvidia's processors are widely used in data centres and computing infrastructure that train and operate AI models. Its most advanced chips have also come under the spotlight because of US export curbs designed to restrict China's access to cutting-edge semiconductor technology.Nvidia announced the probe on Sunday, following Huang's admission that he had been intimate with a business executive whom US intelligence agencies had reportedly identified as someone collecting information for China, according to The New York Times.The New York Times identified Alice Huang as a former executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data centre company whose website prominently highlights its partnership with Nvidia.Nvidia ranks among the world's most valuable publicly listed companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft. Its chip sales to China have periodically faced restrictions from US regulators seeking to curb Beijing's access to advanced technology.“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy according to AP report.“Those questions require evidence rather than speculation,” he added in a text message to reporters.In recent years, Huang has pressed Washington to ease restrictions on Nvidia's chip exports to China. This year, he secured US President Donald Trump's approval to sell the company's H200 chips to the country. However, it remains uncertain whether Beijing will permit Chinese companies to purchase these processors in substantial volumes.In a regulatory filing in August, Nvidia disclosed that it had sold only a limited quantity of chips to China, citing restrictions imposed by the Chinese government on such purchases.Although the H200 is not among Nvidia's most advanced chip models, it remains a sophisticated processor. Huang had earlier also lobbied Trump for permission to sell the company's less advanced H20 chips, which were specifically designed to comply with US export restrictions on China.China's Foreign Ministry rejected the espionage allegations on Monday, describing them as a smear campaign directed at Beijing.The development has plunged the US chipmaker, a key player in the global artificial intelligence industry, into an unprecedented crisis.The company also lacks a clearly identified successor to its chief executive.The more serious concern is the allegation that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”Nvidia's board has launched an investigation and maintained that it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.”The controversy has surfaced at a particularly difficult moment for the company.Democrats secured control of Congress last week, while candidates advocating closer oversight of artificial intelligence and data-centre construction recorded significant victories.Nvidia was already facing the possibility of tougher congressional scrutiny over whether its advanced chips were reaching China. The latest allegations involving Huang have given lawmakers from both parties further grounds to examine the company.One would assume that an internal probe in a tech giant in the US would have no impact whatsoever on Indian stock markets.But, Sensex and Nifty which have delivered negative returns in the last year may actually benefit indirectly from this development. Globally stock markets have rallied on the artificial intelligence and chip-led boom with Nvidia actually leading the rally.India on the other hand has missed out on the AI stock boom, one of the major factors cited for exit of foreign investors from the stock market.But after months of underperformance, Indian equities have recently regained investor interest as concerns grow over concentrated investments in AI. Investors are increasingly looking towards factors such as lower crude oil prices and robust domestic corporate earnings. Last week, India emerged as one of Asia's most prominent beneficiaries of the so-called anti-AI trade.The positive sentiment towards Indian equities received another boost on Monday, with two more banks turning bullish on the market. HSBC upgraded Indian stocks to overweight from neutral, while Citigroup increased its 12-month target for the Nifty 50.Nvidia is at the heart of the AI investment boom and has increasingly relied on its own balance sheet and credit strength to support faster infrastructure spending.Bloomberg Opinion columnist Shuli Ren has described Huang as the “central banker of AI.” The question she raises is particularly relevant now: Will Nvidia's money keep flowing now that the central banker himself is in trouble?According to a Bloomberg analysis, while Huang's troubles alone are not a sufficient basis for an investment case for India, but if the controversy deepens doubts about the AI trade and prompts investors to diversify beyond it, Indian equities could benefit from an unusual advantage that the country does not have a giant, expensive AI sector.
Article Summary: N Nvidia, one of the most valuable listed companies in the world, is in the eye of the storm. The company has launched an investigation into reports that its chief executive, Jensen Huang, had been the “target of a foreign intelligence effort” Nvidia shares dropped 8% at the start of trading on Monday.

Article Title: Anthropic's $1.4 trillion IPO: Price band, listing, investors & more; all you need to know
Article Text:
Anthropic's $1.4 trillion IPO

Anthropic IPO: Valuation, price band, issue size and listing date

Biggest techs backing Anthropic

Investor Investment and association Amazon Has invested at least $13 billion and agreed in April to invest up to another $20 billion. Anthropic has committed to spending more than $100 billion on Amazon's cloud services over 10 years. Google (Alphabet) Has committed up to $40 billion, including an initial $10 billion investment announced in April. It also provides cloud infrastructure and AI chips used to train and run Claude models. Microsoft Has agreed to purchase $1 billion of Anthropic's non-voting shares in the concurrent private placement. Nvidia Has agreed to purchase $10 billion of non-voting shares alongside the listing. AMD Has agreed to purchase $2.5 billion of non-voting shares. Broadcom Has agreed to purchase $1 billion of non-voting shares and is involved in financing and equipment leasing arrangements linked to Anthropic's AI infrastructure. Micron Technology Has agreed to purchase $1 billion of non-voting shares. TSMC Partners Has agreed to purchase $500 million of non-voting shares.

Anthropic’s financial portfolio

Anthropic and AI risks — What experts are saying

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

The artificial intelligence (AI) boom is heading for another major test on Wall Street as Anthropic, the parent company of Claude, prepares for a mega IPO targeting a valuation of $1.4 trillion.Backed by technology giants such as Amazon, Google, Nvidia and AMD, the company has seen its valuation climb rapidly. Its proposed listing will test whether public market investors share the enthusiasm that has fuelled massive investments in AI, particularly as questions grow over how quickly companies can turn their spending into profits.The shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT, Reuters reported.Here's what investors need to know about the proposed listing, the company's backers, its growth prospects and the risks surrounding the AI boom.Anthropic is targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, with reports suggesting its bankers are preparing to increase the figure to $1.5 trillion or more.The company plans to sell 825 million shares at $70-78 apiece, with the IPO expected to raise up to $64.4 billion. A separate private placement with cornerstone investors could bring in another $26 billion, taking the potential fundraising to $90.4 billion.At the top end of the proposed price range, Anthropic would be valued at around $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis. This includes securities such as stock options and restricted stock. Excluding these, its valuation would be close to $1 trillion.If the offering is priced at the midpoint of the proposed range, it could raise more than $61 billion.The initial terms circulated to investment banks had suggested that the IPO could raise as much as $69.3 billion. However, the updated prospectus filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission contained a lower price range and a reduced fundraising target.The shares are expected to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT.Anthropic has attracted some of the biggest names in technology and finance, both as long-term investors and participants in its upcoming private placement.Some of its key technology backers include:Beyond technology companies, Anthropic has received substantial backing from venture capital firms and institutional investors across multiple funding rounds. These include Spark Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Fidelity Management & Research, Salesforce Ventures, ICONIQ, GIC, Coatue Management, D1 Capital Partners, Sequoia Capital, Altimeter Capital and Menlo Ventures.Among individual investors, Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn led Anthropic's first institutional funding round, a $124 million Series A in 2021. Former Google chief executive Eric Schmidt has also personally backed the company.Anthropic's proposed listing could rank among the biggest IPOs ever, although it is expected to fall short of the $86 billion raised by SpaceX in June at a valuation of nearly $1.75 trillion.The company was last valued at $965 billion in a private funding round. Its proposed IPO valuation of up to $1.4 trillion would mark a significant jump.Its valuation is being supported by rapid growth in demand for its products, particularly its Claude models.According to its IPO filing, the company's run-rate revenue stood at roughly $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30.A regulatory filing last month showed that Anthropic generated more than $16 billion in revenue during the first half of the year, around 14 times its revenue in the corresponding period last year.However, the company has yet to turn a profit.Its expansion also requires enormous computing capacity. Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners, including Amazon and Google's parent Alphabet.The IPO could provide the company with significant funds to accelerate its expansion and potentially add billions of dollars to the fortunes of chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister and co-founder Daniela Amodei.Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI leaders and is headed by Dario Amodei. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead underwriters for the offering.Despite strong demand for AI, investors are questioning whether heavy spending on models, data centres and computing infrastructure will generate adequate returns. Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX's AI division have all lost more money than they have made, while elevated borrowing costs and regulatory concerns have added to market uncertainty. A recent Wall Street sell-off also hit stocks linked to AI infrastructure.Anthropic's IPO prospectus flags the technology's potential risks, including faster-moving competitors and safety measures failing to keep pace with AI advances. CEO Dario Amodei has called for slower development, warning in September that AI agents could take over the entire internet within six to 12 months without stronger safeguards.The proposed valuation has also drawn scrutiny from experts. "Anthropic could become an exceptionally successful company, but at this valuation, much of that success is already reflected in the price," Varun Datta, venture capitalist and founder of Truth Ventures told Reuters.Jeff Zell, senior research analyst at IPO Boutique, said the pricing could leave room for investors to bid up the shares. "By seeking a valuation close to 20% below 'market expectations', this allows investors to 'bid up' the IPO rather than facing a take-it-or-leave-it scenario like SpaceX took," he said.
Article Summary: Anthropic is targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. The company plans to sell 825 million shares at $70-78 apiece. The shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT.

Article Title: Indian Railways steps up cleanliness checks on 11 trains with journey times of over 40 hours, staff to photograph coaches and toilets at key stops; Vivek Express, Jhelum Express on the list
Article Text:
The depots responsible for these trains will closely track cleanliness and maintenance.

Long-distance trains in focus

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the new cleanliness measures for long-distance trains will improve passenger satisfaction? Yes, definitely No, I don't think so 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Indian Railways bets on waste disposal

Long-distance train journeys can sometimes be cumbersome especially on account of cleanliness in trains. The Railway Board has recently prepared a plan to tighten supervision and intensify cleanliness measures on long-distance trains that take more than 40 hours to complete their journeys.Officials have said that 11 trains have been selected under the initiative, with staff required to take photographs of coaches and toilets bearing time stamps at the starting station, destination and specified inspection points along the route.The depots responsible for these trains will closely track cleanliness and maintenance, while zonal railway officials will review passenger complaints and the action taken to resolve them every week, they said.The performance of agencies providing on-board housekeeping services will also be evaluated based on complaints lodged through Rail Madad, the Railways' official digital platform."The on-board housekeeping staff in these trains will be trained to take up small repairs. Dedicated teams comprising plumbers, electrical staff and other requisite maintenance personnel may be deployed en route these trains to speedily address concerns," a senior official recently told ET.The official added that cleaning at designated 'clean train station' points would receive particular attention."Divisions have been asked to ensure adequate manpower, equipment and consumables," the official added.The 11 trains covered by the plan are Jhelum Express, Pune-Saharsa Express, Amritsar Garib Rath Express, Avadh Assam Express, Howrah-Yesvantpur Express, Vivek Express, Danapur-SMVT Bengaluru Express, Amrapali Express, Ahmedabad-Saharsa Express, Rajgir-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus Express and RKMP-Agartala Express.Indian Railways has put in place a comprehensive system to collect, process and dispose of waste generated at railway stations and aboard trains. Stations have been equipped with twin dustbins to facilitate waste collection and segregation at the source.Waste produced during train journeys is gathered at designated waste-handling stations at regular intervals. These stations have arrangements with Urban Local Bodies and municipal authorities to ensure its proper disposal.Depending on operational requirements, Indian Railways has also installed waste-processing facilities at various stations, including biogas and composting plants, as well as plastic bottle-crushing machines.Following the applicability of the new Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, and directions issued by the Supreme Court, the Railways has undertaken several initiatives to strengthen waste management across its establishments.The Railway Board has issued a Standard Operating Procedure (SoP) for solid waste management across railway stations, trains, railway colonies, hospitals, workshops, production units and other railway establishments. The guidelines lay down procedures for waste segregation, collection, transportation, processing and scientific disposal. They also specify monitoring arrangements and clearly define responsibilities at different levels of the administration.Zonal Railways have begun identifying units that fall under the category of bulk waste generators as defined by the SWM Rules, 2026. An “As-is Waste Characterization and Quantification Study” has also been planned to evaluate the existing volume and composition of waste generated across Indian Railways' establishments and trains.Dedicated nodal officers have been appointed by Zonal Railways to draw up comprehensive waste management plans, carry out periodic audits, oversee implementation and submit regular compliance reports to the Railway Board. Divisions have also been instructed to formulate their own action plans to improve waste management. In addition, dedicated Environment & Housekeeping Management (EnHM) departments have been set up at the divisional, zonal and Railway Board levels to oversee waste management-related issues.To maintain cleanliness and hygiene throughout train journeys, Indian Railways provides on-board housekeeping services (OBHS) on 1,450 pairs of identified long-distance trains.The Clean Train Station (CTS) scheme is operational at 63 stations and covers 2,800 trains. Under this arrangement, dedicated teams equipped with cleaning equipment use the scheduled halts to clean coach toilets and washbasins and remove garbage from dustbins inside the trains.
Article Summary: Indian Railways has put in place a comprehensive system to collect, process and dispose of waste generated at railway stations and aboard trains. Stations have been equipped with twin dustbins to facilitate waste collection and segregation at the source. Indian Railways provides on-board housekeeping services (HS) on 2,800 pairs of trains.

Article Title: Insurer rejected Rs 30 lakh accidental death claim citing alcohol consumption; consumer commission finds medical record discrepancies and upholds payout with 9% interest and Rs 75,000 as compensation
Article Text:
The family contested the insurer's decision before the District Consumer Commission, Vellore. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the family win the case against the insurer?

IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company Ltd.

v. Pearl Beverages Ltd.

Insurance payouts can sometimes be tricky if the insurer denies claims. In one such case, a pensioner died following a road accident and his wife and two daughters turned to the accidental death insurance cover associated with his pension account for financial assistance.However, the insurer declined their claim, citing a policy clause excluding certain injuries linked to alcohol consumption. The family challenged the insurer's decision and won relief.A pensioner held coverage under a group personal accident/salary package/pension account policy issued by the insurer through the man’s bank account.The insurance policy covered the period from January 4, 2022, to January 3, 2023. On April 9, 2022, the man was involved in a motor accident and suffered severe head injuries. He was taken to a hospital, where he died on April 18, 2022.His wife and two daughters filed a claim for the insured amount of Rs 30 lakh on December 5, 2022. The insurer however, rejected their request on January 9, 2023, relying on a policy exclusion concerning injuries sustained under the influence of alcohol.“The insurer relied on the policy exclusion for being under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs or other intoxicants except where the insured is not directly responsible for the injury/accident though under influence of intoxication,” says Vishal Jain, Founder and Senior Partner at Ayaam Legal.The family contested the insurer's decision before the District Consumer Commission, Vellore. They argued that it had repudiated the claim without presenting credible medical or scientific evidence to establish that the man was intoxicated at the time of the accident.The District Commission ruled in the family's favour, directing the insurer to settle the insurance claim and pay interest and compensation for deficiency in service and mental agony. The insurer then appealed against the order before the Tamil Nadu State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.The State Commission upheld the District Commission's order directing the insurer to settle the accidental death insurance claim of Rs 30 lakh.The insurer was also ordered to pay annual interest at 9% from September 1, 2023, until the date of the District Commission's order. In addition, the family was awarded Rs 50,000 as compensation for deficiency in service and mental agony, along with Rs 25,000 towards litigation expenses.The Commission found several significant gaps in the evidence presented by the insurer.According to Vivek Kumar, Advocate, Delhi High Court, the insurer based its decision partly on a hospital death summary that stated that the deceased was under the influence of alcohol when the incident occurred.However, the Commission noted that the medical document did not clarify the basis for this statement. It was unclear whether the information came from the deceased himself, an accompanying person, the police or another medico-legal source, or an independent clinical assessment by the treating doctor.The Commission stressed that recording a patient's history of alcohol consumption does not, by itself, establish that the person was under the influence of alcohol at the relevant time.The insurer also cited a reported plasma alcohol level of 106.1 mg/dL. However, the insurer did not submit the original laboratory report to establish the identity and nature of the blood specimen, when it had been collected, which laboratory had tested it, the relevant report or sample number, or whether the test result could be linked to the deceased.The Commission observed that a numerical reading, even when stated with precision, cannot automatically be accepted as scientifically established evidence unless its source and authenticity are demonstrated.Another important aspect of the ruling was the Commission's examination of the two death summaries placed before it by the parties. One of the most significant inconsistencies concerned the date of death. The document relied upon by the insurer recorded April 11, 2022, as the date of death. However, the admitted facts and the medical record submitted by the complainants established that the man had died on April 18, 2022, Kumar told ET.According to the Commission, such discrepancies had a material bearing on the reliability of the documents, the identification of the records and their chronological traceability.The Commission also reiterated that an insurer seeking to reject a claim by invoking an exclusion clause must establish the factual circumstances required for that exclusion to apply. The burden was not on the family to explain or disprove every inconsistency left unresolved in the insurer's documents.The Commission further referred to the Supreme Court's judgment in, AIR 2021 SC 2277. The ruling clarifies that an insurer is not required in every case to produce a breathalyser reading or a blood-alcohol test report to establish that an exclusion applies. The conclusion can instead be based on the totality of reliable circumstances, Kumar explains.However, this does not absolve an insurer of the responsibility to establish that the insured was actually under the influence of alcohol.
Article Summary: A pensioner died following a road accident and his wife and two daughters turned to the accidental death insurance cover associated with his pension account for financial assistance. The insurer declined their claim, citing a policy clause excluding certain injuries linked to alcohol consumption. The family challenged the insurer's decision and won relief.

Article Title: Moody’s raises India’s FY27 growth forecast to 7% on strong economic momentum
Article Text:
Representative image

Inflation, monsoon pose risks to growth

Energy diversification supports economic resilience

Global agencies raise India growth projections

Moody’s Ratings has raised its growth forecast for the Indian economy to 7% for the current financial year, from its earlier estimate of 6.5%, citing broad-based economic momentum and the country’s resilience to the energy supply shock linked to the Iran war.In its Global Macro Outlook 2027-28, the US-based rating agency said robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals should help India sustain growth near 7% over the medium term."India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7 per cent from 6.5 per cent," Moody’s said.The agency, however, flagged near-term risks to the growth outlook, including rising price pressures on household consumption, a deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions that could weigh on agricultural output and rural demand.Moody’s said household consumption remained vulnerable to "intensifying and broadening price pressures", with headline inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) target range of 2-6%.A weak monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions could further affect farm output and rural demand, it said.Tighter monetary policy also poses a potential risk to investment. "With the RBI on track to raise rates further, tighter monetary policy could delay the recovery in private investment," Moody’s added.India’s central bank raised interest rates for the first time in nearly four years in October.Economists polled by Reuters expect headline consumer inflation to rise to 5.93% in October, close to the upper end of the RBI’s tolerance band.The inflation data is due on Thursday. Markets currently anticipate another 90 basis points of monetary tightening over the next 12 months, Reuters reported.Moody’s said a sustained private investment boom that significantly boosts manufacturing, employment and productivity could push growth above its baseline projections.The agency said India had adjusted to the energy price shock better than previously anticipated, helped by its ability to diversify crude oil and gas supplies.State-backed oil marketing companies and tax cuts had also helped shield consumers from the immediate impact of higher energy prices, it said.India’s large refining capacity, including the world's biggest single-site refining complex, has helped limit fuel supply disruptions while supporting its position as a major exporter of refined petroleum products, Moody’s added.High-frequency indicators point to a possible revival in private capital expenditure. Robust capital goods production and imports, accelerating industrial credit growth and rising capacity utilisation suggest that India may be approaching a new private investment cycle after several years of corporate and banking sector balance-sheet repair, the agency said.Broader economic activity also remained solid, supported by expanding manufacturing and services purchasing managers' indexes. Goods and services tax collections, vehicle sales and merchandise exports recorded double-digit year-on-year growth, according to Moody’s.India’s economy grew 7.8% year-on-year in the April-June quarter, according to official data, with investment and manufacturing strength adding to consumer demand.Moody’s revision follows a series of upgrades to India's growth outlook by other international institutions and rating agencies.The Asian Development Bank and S&P had raised their projections for the current financial year to 7%, from 6.6% earlier, while Fitch had revised its estimate to 6.9%. The OECD had projected growth of 7.1%, up from 6.3% in its June outlook.The World Bank also raised its forecast for India's 2026-27 growth to 7.1% from 6.6% in a report published last month, citing strong domestic demand and exports despite global headwinds. It projected growth of 7.2% for 2027-28.The World Bank had also flagged risks from global oil prices, El Nino and potential stock market corrections that could trigger volatility in capital flows.
Article Summary: Moody’s Ratings has raised its growth forecast for the Indian economy to 7% for the current financial year, from its earlier estimate of 6.5%. The agency, however, flagged near-term risks to the growth outlook, including rising price pressures on household consumption and a deficient southwest monsoon.

Article Title: Mother Dairy, Amul milk gets costlier: Dairy giant hikes rate by upto Rs 6 per litre from Thursday; check prices
Article Text:
Mother Dairy raises prices

Why are milk prices increasing?

How much will milk cost now?

Full cream milk (packaged): Rs 76 per litre, up from Rs 72.

Rs 76 per litre, up from Rs 72. Toned milk (bulk vended): Rs 60 per litre, up from Rs 58.

Rs 60 per litre, up from Rs 58. Toned milk (packaged): Rs 62 per litre, up from Rs 60.

Rs 62 per litre, up from Rs 60. Double-toned milk: Rs 56 per litre, up from Rs 54.

Rs 56 per litre, up from Rs 54. Cow milk: Rs 65 per litre, up from Rs 62.

Rs 65 per litre, up from Rs 62. Full cream buffalo milk: Rs 86 per litre, up from Rs 80.

Nandini had also raised milk prices in Karnataka

NEW DELHI: Milk is set to get costlier in Delhi NCR from November 12, with dairy companies Mother Dairy and Amul increasing prices by Rs 2 to Rs 6 per litre. The price hike comes amid lower milk supplies and higher costs of buying milk from farmers.The increase will vary across milk varieties. Toned milk will cost Rs 2 more per litre, full cream milk Rs 4 more and full cream buffalo milk Rs 6 more, according to industry sources.In Delhi-NCR, full cream packaged milk will now cost Rs 76 per litre, compared with Rs 72 earlier. Packaged toned milk will cost Rs 62, up from Rs 60, while toned milk sold through bulk vending machines will cost Rs 60 against Rs 58 earlier.Double-toned milk will become costlier from Rs 54 to Rs 56 per litre. Cow milk prices will rise from Rs 62 to Rs 65, while full cream buffalo milk, which contains 6.5% fat, will cost Rs 86 against Rs 80 earlier.Mother Dairy, the largest milk supplier in Delhi-NCR, had last increased prices on May 14, 2026.Milk procurement has become more expensive for dairy companies. Milk fat prices have risen by around 20-25% over the past few months, while higher cattle feed prices have added to farmers' costs.Milk supplies have also tightened despite the flush season, when production and availability usually improve. The shortage has affected the availability of milk fat, making it more expensive for dairy companies.When fresh milk supplies fall short, companies usually use milk powder and milk fat to prepare liquid milk. However, higher milk fat prices have also increased the cost of this process.Dairy companies have raised the prices they pay farmers to encourage them to produce and supply more milk. Amul has increased the procurement rate linked to milk fat to Rs 1,000 per kilogram. This allows farmers to receive more than Rs 60 per litre for milk, according to industry sources.Mother Dairy has decided to pass on part of these higher costs to consumers. The company pays farmers 75-80% of the money it earns from milk sales, sources told PTI.Here are the revised prices of different milk varieties in Delhi-NCR:Mother Dairy sells around 35 lakh litres of milk every day in Delhi-NCR through its outlets, general trade and e-commerce platforms. Its total daily milk sales across markets exceed 50 lakh litres.The company reported a 17% rise in turnover to Rs 20,300 crore in the last fiscal year. The growth was driven by higher demand for its milk products and cooking oils.Started in 1974, Mother Dairy is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB). It sells milk and milk products under the Mother Dairy brand, edible oils under Dhara, and fresh fruits and vegetables, frozen vegetables, snacks, pulps and concentrates under Safal.Before the latest increase by Mother Dairy and Amul, Nandini had raised milk prices in Karnataka. The state Cabinet approved an Rs 8 per litre increase in the base price, with the new rates taking effect from November 1.The Karnataka government said the increase was needed to protect dairy farmers facing severe drought conditions. Law and parliamentary affairs minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the revised prices were still within the range charged in most other states.He also said rising prices of other goods had hurt farmers and milk supply in Karnataka had fallen by 10 lakh litres due to the drought this year.Cooperation minister Laxman Savadi said the government also had to consider the possibility of farmers selling their milk to other states if prices were not increased. This could have led to a shortage of milk in Karnataka.Under the revised arrangement, Rs 7 of the Rs 8 per litre increase was to go to farmers, while Re 1 was allocated to milk unions in the state.
Article Summary: Mother Dairy and Amul raise prices by Rs 2 to Rs 6 per litre in Delhi-NCR. Milk fat prices have risen by around 20-25% over the past few months. Milk supplies have also tightened despite the flush season, when production usually improves.

Article Title: India-UK trade deal faces early test as customs hold scotch imports over tariff row
Article Text:
Representative image

Finance ministry memo backs 150% duty

More than 80 containers of Pernod, Diageo held

Indian customs authorities are holding dozens of containers of bulk Scotch whisky imported by Pernod Ricard and Diageo as investigators insist that the shipments attract a 150% import duty, despite assurances from the commerce ministry that the lower tariff under the India-UK trade pact would be honoured.The dispute centres on whether bulk Scotch concentrates used to manufacture whisky brands qualify for the reduced 75% duty introduced under the trade agreement, which came into effect in July.Customs investigators argue that the concession applies only to finished products, such as bottled, ready-to-drink Scotch, and not to concentrates that undergo further processing.Following lobbying by the industry, the commerce ministry assured senior executives on November 2 that India would honour the trade pact and seek an early resolution. The assurance initially led liquor companies, including Pernod Ricard and Diageo, to expect that the lower tariff would be applied.However, a confidential November 4 memo from the finance ministry's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), reviewed by Reuters, instructed customs commissioners across the country to continue applying the higher duty.The DRI memo said importers were "incorrectly" claiming benefits under the India-UK trade pact for bulk Scotch shipments.It said the products should attract a 150% tariff under a customs classification introduced on May 1 for "compound alcoholic preparations".The memo warned that any misclassification had "large-scale, recurring substantial revenue implications" and directed customs officials to ensure the correct application of the higher duty."Preliminary investigation revealed that the imported goods are not finished whisky/brand/rum as such, but are concentrates/compound preparations which are subjected to further manufacturing," the memo said.A senior finance ministry source told Reuters that the finance and commerce ministries were discussing an appropriate resolution of the matter.The customs dispute has left shipments belonging to the two companies held at Indian ports, with both unwilling to pay the higher duty, according to four people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters.Pernod Ricard and Diageo each have more than 40 containers held at ports, two industry sources said. Bacardi has another five containers on hold, a third source said.The prolonged delays could disrupt supplies, the sources said. In recent weeks, tax officials have also searched the offices of several companies, including Pernod Ricard and Diageo, and questioned executives.About 80% of Scotch whisky imports from Britain by volume arrive in bulk and are subsequently used to manufacture Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL), which blends smaller quantities of Scotch with other spirits and ingredients.Scotch exports to India were worth $335 million in 2024. The Scotch Whisky Association has estimated that the India-UK trade agreement could increase the value of this trade by $1.34 billion over five years.The International Spirits and Wines Association of India has privately cautioned New Delhi that the dispute "risks undermining, in practice, an important market-access benefit negotiated and agreed between India and the United Kingdom".Tariff disputes have previously been a source of friction for foreign investors in India, with multinational companies facing demands for substantial back-tax payments. Similar disputes have involved companies such as Samsung and Volkswagen.
Article Summary: Customs authorities are holding dozens of containers of bulk Scotch whisky imported by Pernod Ricard and Diageo. Investigators insist that the shipments attract a 150% import duty. Dispute centres on whether bulk Scotch concentrates used to manufacture whisky brands qualify for the reduced 75% duty.

Article Title: Blackstone to buy 16% in IIFL Finance for Rs 5,000 crore: What's the deal all about
Article Text:
Blackstone's Rs 5,000 crore bet on IIFL Finance

Breaking down the Blackstone deal

Where will the fresh capital go?

IIFL Finance's portfolio

Global investment firm Blackstone is set to buy nearly 16% stake in IIFL Finance for Rs 5,000 crore. The investment is part of a larger Rs 6,414 crore fundraise approved by the company's board on Tuesday.The deal will make Blackstone a key investor in the non-bank lender, which plans to use the fresh capital to strengthen its finances and expand its lending business, particularly gold loans and credit to small businesses.The Rs 6,414 crore fundraise will come from three investors. Blackstone will contribute Rs 5,000 crore, while IIFL Finance's promoters, Nirmal Jain and R Venkataraman, will invest Rs 1,264 crore. Anchorage Capital will put in another Rs 150 crore.According to the company's stock exchange filing, funds managed by Blackstone Private Equity will invest through a preferential allotment of compulsorily convertible preference shares. These shares will be converted into equity shares at Rs 602 apiece within 18 months of allotment.After the conversion, Blackstone will hold approximately 16% of IIFL Finance on a fully diluted basis.Blackstone will also get representation on the company's board. However, the existing promoters will continue as co-promoters, and IIFL Finance has clarified that the deal will not lead to a change in control.The fresh capital is expected to improve the company's financial position and give it more room to grow its lending business.IIFL Finance expects its capital adequacy ratio to rise to around 30% from nearly 17%, based on September 2026 figures. The additional funds will mainly support its secured lending businesses, particularly gold finance, along with lending to small businesses.The company also plans to invest more in technology and expand its co-lending partnerships with banks. It said the stronger capital base could help improve its credit ratings and lower borrowing costs over time.Welcoming Blackstone as an investor, IIFL Finance Founder and Managing Director Nirmal Jain said, "We are delighted to welcome Blackstone as a partner in IIFL Finance. Their investment is a strong endorsement of the franchise our team has built, and of the opportunity to bring formal, secured credit to millions of underserved households and small businesses across India."Jain added, "The investment strengthens our balance sheet and gives us the headroom to scale our franchises, invest further in technology, and deepen our co-lending partnerships with banks, while staying disciplined on risk and capital."IIFL Finance had assets under management of Rs 1.24 lakh crore on a consolidated basis as of September-end. Its gross non-performing assets stood at 1.5% of total loans, down 7 basis points from three months earlier.Blackstone's investment comes amid a series of deals involving global financial firms and Indian lenders.Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings has proposed buying a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank. Bank of America has bought a 49.9% stake in the non-bank lending arm of Jio Financial Services, while Japan's MUFG has invested in Shriram Finance. Dubai-based Emirates NBD has also agreed to buy a 60% stake in RBL Bank.The proposed investment in IIFL Finance is subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals.
Article Summary: IIFL Finance plans to use fresh capital to strengthen its finances and expand its lending business. Blackstone will contribute Rs 5,000 crore, while IIFL Finance's promoters, Nirmal Jain and R Venkataraman, will invest Rs 1,264 crore.

Article Title: Rupee rises 7 paise to 93.70 against US dollar as foreign inflows support sentiment
Article Text:
Rupee strengthens below 94/$

NEW DELHI: Rupee began Wednesday on a strong note, gaining 7 paise to 93.70 against the US dollar in early trade. The momentum is supported by renewed foreign fund inflows, softer crude oil prices and improving geopolitical sentiment.Rupee has emerged as one of Asia's best-performing currencies in FY27. Forex traders said the gradual return of foreign investors to Indian markets, following months of cautious participation and significant outflows, has helped support the rupee.In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at around 93.71 before gaining further to touch 93.70, up 7 paise from its previous closing level on Monday.Domestic equity, currency and debt markets remained closed on Tuesday on account of 'Diwali Balipratipada'. In the previous trading session on Monday, the rupee had gained 21 paise to close at 93.77 against the US dollar.CR Forex Advisors MD Amit Pabari said rupee's positive momentum was being supported by the steady return of foreign capital, softer crude prices and improving geopolitical sentiment."The rupee's underlying momentum remains positive, backed by a steady return of foreign capital, softer crude prices and improving geopolitical sentiment.If these supportive factors continue, USD/INR could extend its decline towards 93.50, with 93.00 emerging as the next important level to watch," Pabari said.Meanwhile, the dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 102.26, up 0.03 per cent.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 1.01 per cent higher at USD 92.41 per barrel in futures trade.Commenting on the factors influencing the domestic currency, Anindya Banerjee , Head of Commodity and Currency Research at Kotak NEO, said cheaper oil prices offered support to the rupee by reducing the import bill. However, higher US yields and a stronger dollar continued to exert pressure."For the rupee, cheaper oil offers support through a lower import bill, while higher US yields and the stronger dollar create an opposing pressure," Banerjee said.He added that India's inflation data, scheduled to be released on Thursday, would be the next domestic policy signal.Foreign investment flows have also provided support to domestic markets. According to exchange data, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 7,212.22 crore on Monday.Foreign investors have turned net buyers of Indian equities in November, investing Rs 53,739 crore in the first nine days of the month, following two consecutive months of outflows.The buying has been driven by the AI-led sell-off in global markets, strong domestic earnings growth and attractive valuations of large-cap stocks.The latest inflows come after foreign investors withdrew Rs 34,843 crore in October and Rs 35,861 crore in September, according to data available with the depositories.
Article Summary: Rupee has emerged as one of Asia's best-performing currencies in FY27. Forex traders said the gradual return of foreign investors to Indian markets has helped support the rupee.Domestic equity, currency and debt markets remained closed on Tuesday on account of 'Diwali Balipratipada'

Article Title: Sensex ends 770 points higher after eight-month high opening! Investors get Rs 5.25 lakh crore richer - what's fueling the rally
Article Text:
Stock market rallies to 8-month high - key reasons fueling the rally

Key triggers behind the market rally:

FIIs return to Indian equities

Nvidia probe puts the AI trade under scrutiny

Crude cools below $100 per barrel

Rupee gains ground against the dollar

Strong Q2 earnings give markets another boost

Banking, auto and pharma stocks lead the sectoral charge

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

NEW DELHI: Dalal Street returned from its Diwali break in a cheerful mood on Wednesday, with benchmark indices climbing to levels last seen eight months ago, in February. Sensex jumped over 1,300 points during early trade, while Nifty50 crossed the 25,300 mark as buying spread across sectors.BSE Sensex opened at 82,250.52, up 1,143.87 points or 1.41%, while NSE Nifty50 started at 25,337.80, gaining 293.15 points or 1.17%. Both benchmarks touched their highest opening levels since February 27.The rally also made investors richer by around Rs 5.25 lakh crore. The total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies rose to Rs 5,12,51,866 crore from Rs 5,07,26,775.40 crore in the previous sessionHowever, BSE Sensex pared some of its gains but closed 772.75 points, or 0.95%, higher at 81,879.40 while Nifty50 ended 210.40 points, or 0.84%, higher at 25,255.05.All 16 major sectoral indices opened higher, while the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 0.64% and 0.72%, respectively.Foreign institutional investors (FIIs), who had been net sellers of Indian equities, have returned to Dalal Street with aggressive buying. They invested Rs 53,170 crore in the first six trading sessions of the month, emerging as one of the biggest triggers behind the market's recent rally.V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist, Geojit Investments, told ANI, "Nifty 50 has surged by 8.6% in just six trading days of this month. This surge was triggered mainly by the aggressive FII buying of Rs 53170 crores so far this month. The dramatic change in the market environment was triggered by positive global cues for India from the weakening of the AI trade."The shift in global cues, particularly the weakening of the AI trade, has helped change the investment environment for Indian equities. Vijayakumar expects foreign investors to maintain their buying momentum, providing further support to large-cap stocks.He further added, "Given the new favourable environment for the Indian market, FIIs are likely to continue buying, imparting resilience to the frontline stocks in banking/financials, telecom, capital goods, select auto and pharmaceutical majors. This rally, which has more steam left, will be led again by large-caps".Nvidia's probe into allegations that its CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort has added to concerns around the global AI trade. The chipmaker's shares fell 8% on Monday, raising fresh questions about the AI-led market boom.The development appears to have indirectly benefit Indian equities, which have underperformed amid the global rush towards AI and chip stocks. As investors reassess concentrated AI bets, India is attracting fresh interest on the back of easing crude prices and strong domestic earnings. Last week, it emerged as one of Asia's biggest beneficiaries of the so-called 'anti-AI trade'.The shift has also prompted global banks to turn more positive on Indian markets. HSBC upgraded Indian equities to 'overweight' from 'neutral', while Citigroup raised its 12-month target for the Nifty 50.Easing crude oil prices have provided another reason for investors to cheer. Brent crude futures fell to a two-month low of $89.16 per barrel on Tuesday after US officials played down the possibility of additional military action against Iran, easing concerns over potential supply disruptions.Prices recovered marginally on Wednesday, rising 0.5% to around $92 per barrel. Brent was trading at $92.41 in the commodities market, up around 1%. However, prices remained well below the levels seen earlier during the conflict.The moderation in crude prices has supported sentiment in Indian equities, with the recent decline offering a more favourable backdrop for domestic markets.Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said, "Indian equities appear well positioned to extend their recent advance, with a sustained moderation in crude oil prices and a revival in foreign portfolio inflows providing a more supportive backdrop for domestic markets."Rupee’s momentum has added to the positive mood in the currency and equity markets. It opened 20 paise stronger against the US dollar to 93.70 against the US dollar.Forex traders said that foreign investors were gradually finding their way back into the domestic market after months of cautious participation and substantial outflows.Rupee has emerged as one of Asia's best-performing currencies in FY27. Continued foreign fund inflows could provide an important cushion against external uncertainties, traders said.The currency's appreciation, along with renewed foreign buying and easing oil prices, has helped improve sentiment towards Indian equities. The Sensex and Nifty have gained around 10% so far this month.Beyond the buying frenzy, better-than-expected Q2 earnings have provided the rally with fundamental support. Nifty 50 companies recorded nearly 24% earnings growth in the second quarter, their highest in 12 quarters.Better-than-expected September-quarter earnings have added to the optimism, with 181 companies reporting a more than doubling of net profit year-on-year in Q2 FY27. Stronger demand, improved margins and a recovery across sectors including banking, metals, pharmaceuticals, energy and manufacturing have helped India Inc regain earnings momentum.The list includes major companies such as Indian Oil Corporation, JSW Steel, Hindustan Zinc, Adani Power, GAIL and Vedanta, alongside newer businesses such as Nykaa parent FSN E-Commerce Ventures, Paytm parent One97 Communications and Lenskart.The market rally was broad-based, with banking, automobile and pharmaceutical stocks among the major gainers during early trade.The Nifty Private Bank index advanced 1.39%, while the Nifty PSU Bank index gained 1.18%. The Nifty Auto index rose 1.15% and the Nifty Pharma index climbed 1%.Other sectors also joined the advance. The Nifty FMCG index gained 0.91%, while the Nifty IT and Nifty Metal indices rose 0.84% and 0.34%, respectively.The broader market also participated in the rally. The Nifty 100 advanced 1.12%, while the mid-cap and small-cap indices recorded gains, showing that buying interest was not limited to frontline stocks.Meanwhile, the positive sentiment extended to other Asian markets on Wednesday, with most regional indices trading in the green. Taiwan's Weighted Index led the gains, rising 1.90% to 43,514. South Korea's KOSPI advanced 1.70% to 5,327, while Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 1.32% to 61,258. Singapore's Straits Times index edged up 0.38%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng, however, bucked the regional trend, declining 1% to 24,312.
Article Summary: BSE Sensex opened at 82,250.52, up 1,143.87 points or 1.41%, while NSE Nifty50 started at 25,337.80, gaining 293.15 points or1.17%. Both benchmarks touched their highest opening levels since February 27. The rally also made investors richer by around Rs 5.25 lakh crore.

Article Title: Gen Z saving for home, Gen X for retirement
Article Text:
FDs remain king of fixed income

Chennai

: Did you know that 65% of Indians, who save, begin saving or start investing well before the age of 30? 2026 has been an year of uncertainty, with the RBI projecting consumer price inflation (CPI) of 5.2% for FY27. While markets are gradually gaining stability, a latest survey by YouGov, commissioned by Stable Money in the context of the recent World Savings Day revealed how Indians save, what they save for and where they put their money into?The survey revealed, while Gen Z is saving for a home (26%), Gen X is more focused on retirement (35%). It also showed that nearly half of women savers (56%) call the shots on household money. Mutual funds and fixed deposits are neck and neck at the top: 23% pick MFs first and 21% pick bank FDs and RDs.Interestingly, between the morning commute and the evening scroll, Indians are doing what their parents once did at the bank counter: putting money away, albeit digitally - 80% of Indian savers have gone digital. “Indians always had the habit of saving. That is intact. Today it lives on the phone,” says Saurabh Jain, co-founder, Stable Money.Among women, there is a growing sense of financial independence, thanks to greater access to information via digital platforms. “Research and analysis which was earlier largely provided only by professionals such as financial advisors is now accessible at their fingertips through smartphones, further democratised by AI tools empowering women to compare financial products, assess returns and make more informed investment decisions on their own,” says Nalinakanthi V, partner, SowSampadh Partners, a Chennai-based mutual fund distributor.The report also showed that about 19% prefer fixed income to savings account, and 11% would rather reduce debt, so 87% would invest, save, or pay down debt with it. Only 13% would spend it: 8% on travel or an experience and 5% on a luxury purchase.
Article Summary: 65% of Indians save, begin saving or start investing well before the age of 30. While Gen Z is saving for a home, Gen X is more focused on retirement. Nearly half of women savers call the shots on household money. 80% of Indian savers have gone digital.

Article Title: Ramco plans construction chemicals unit at AP plant
Article Text:
Last year, Ramco Cements unveiled a new brand identity for the business under the name Hard Worker

Chennai

: Ramco Cements plans to invest Rs 20 crore in a new construction chemicals manufacturing unit at its Kolimigundla plant in Andhra Pradesh , even as it sticks to its Rs 800 crore capital expenditure plan for the current fiscal. The company also plans to raise about Rs 150 crore through the sale of non-core assets.The proposed unit for construction chemicals will have an annual production capacity of 1.2 lakh tonnes and is expected to be completed by the second quarter of FY28, according to the company’s investor presentation.Though Ramco has been present in the construction chemicals business for more than two decades, it has sharpened its focus on the segment in recent years, banking on its growth potential. Last year, it unveiled a new brand identity for the business, Hard Worker. The domestic construction chemicals market is projected to reach Rs 40,000 crore by 2030.The company’s construction chemicals sales volume rose to 2.04 lakh tonnes in Q2FY27 from 1.48 lakh tonnes in the year-ago period and 1.35 lakh tonnes in Q1FY27. Revenue from the business grew 31% to Rs 217 crore in the first half of FY27. Ramco has set a target of clocking revenue of Rs 2,000 crore in this business over the next four years.Ramco monetised Rs 1,098 crore through non-core asset sales in the last two years. It has identified further assets worth about Rs 150 crore for disposal in the near term, of which Rs 29 crore was realised in the first half of FY27.The company spent Rs 373 crore on capital expenditure in the first half of FY27, with its full-year capex guidance unchanged at Rs 800 crore.Ramco completed the debottlenecking of its Jayanthipuram plant in Q2 FY27, adding 0.73 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) to its capacity and taking its total cement capacity to 27.17 MTPA.The company aims to increase its cement capacity to about 31 MTPA by March 2027, with the commissioning of Line 2 at Kolimigundla. The 3.15 MTPA clinker unit at the facility is expected to be commissioned ahead of schedule, by December 2026.A 15 MW waste heat recovery system (WHRS) is also expected to be commissioned alongside Line 2, strengthening the company’s capacity to generate green power.
Article Summary: Ramco Cements plans to invest Rs 20 crore in a new construction chemicals manufacturing unit at its Kolimigundla plant in Andhra Pradesh. The company also plans to raise about Rs 150 crore through the sale of non-core assets. The proposed unit for construction chemicals will have an annual production capacity of 1.2 lakh tonnes.

Article Title: Cheaper Scotch raises stakes for desi whisky
Article Text:
Cheaper Scotch raises stakes for desi whisky

BENGALURU: Cheaper Scotch is putting Indian whisky makers under pressure, even as lower import duties offer savings to companies that use it in their blends. For small distillers that make their own spirits, an imported label can now cost substantially less than a locally made bottle.Huli's rice malt whisky was launched in Karnataka at Rs 2,650 for 750ml. By comparison, J&B Rare was priced at Rs 1,375 at Bengaluru retailer Tonique in October, according to TOI's earlier reporting. At these prices, J&B Rare cost Rs 1,275 less, or about half as much. Tonique said the price had fallen from Rs 2,835, attributing the reduction to local bottling."The smaller players will not be able to survive," said Huli Spirits founder Aruna Urs. Her Mysuru distillery makes spirits from locally sourced paddy and jaggery and does not import Scotch.Arun Kumar Parasa of Unistil Alcoblends said falling Scotch prices had adversely affected the Indian single malt industry. Lower duties on bulk Scotch imported by some small and medium distilleries would benefit them "very marginally", he said.The distinction is between making spirits locally and buying imported whisky for bottling or blending.Bulk Scotch arrives in large containers and can be bottled here or used as an ingredient in Indian whisky.A lower import bill can help these manufacturers, while cheaper finished bottles intensify competition for other producers.Jason Holway, senior consultant at drinks research firm IWSR, expects the price gap to narrow further. "Depending on the state, cheaper blended Scotches are expected to become more attractively priced than they used to be and may not be much more expensive than domestic premium brands using Scotch as an ingredient."India's trade agreement with Britain cut Scotch import duties from 150% to 75%. Customs officials subsequently questioned whether certain bulk shipments qualified for the lower duty. On Nov 2, commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal assured manufacturers that the duty benefits would be protected, with commerce and revenue officials to work on resolving the classification dispute.An industry executive, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Indian buyers were also negotiating better purchase prices from Scotland. The executive estimated that the duty reduction could lower retail prices by roughly 8-10%, depending on state taxes and companies' pricing decisions. Distribution difficulties and advertising restrictions remained longstanding hurdles for small manufacturers, the executive added.IWSR's figures also show the limits of India's shift towards expensive whisky. Its premium-and-above category, defined as Rs 2,899.01 or more per 750ml bottle, accounted for less than 1% of whisky consumed by volume in 2025, Holway said.
Article Summary: India's trade agreement with Britain cut Scotch import duties from 150% to 75%. Customs officials questioned whether certain bulk shipments qualified for the lower duty. Lower duties on bulk Scotch imported by some small and medium distilleries would benefit them "very marginally"

Article Title: Tech, heavy engineering lead profit growth in manufacturing
Article Text:
Tech, heavy engineering lead profit growth in manufacturing

NEW DELHI: High-value segments, such as technology, heavy engineering and automotive segments, have led the profit growth in India's organised manufacturing sector in 2024-25, the latest annual survey of industries (ASI) data showed. Despite headwinds, these sectors ensured resilient overall value addition and broader wage distribution across the formal manufacturing sector.Among industries, computer and electronic products recorded a 46% jump in profits to Rs 41,100 crore, alongside a 20% expansion in the wage bill (Rs 33,800 crore). Fabricated metals manufacturing matched this momentum in profits, with a 46% profit jump to Rs 34,180 crore.The ASI data showed that net profit in the overall formal manufacturing sector rose 7.7% in 2024-25 to reach Rs 11.6 lakh crore, while the total wage bill - including salary, bonus and employers' contribution in the form of provident fund - expanded 12.3% to nearly Rs 9 lakh crore.The pharmaceutical industry saw a 24% jump in profits to Rs 1.2 lakh crore, while its wage bill increased 19% to Rs 69,300 crore. Labour intensive industries, which employ a vast majority of the formal manufacturing workforce such as textiles and wearing apparel, saw their profitability rise 34% (Rs 24,232 crore) and 30% (Rs 17,567 crore) respectively.Wage bill for these industries, however, grew moderately. Textiles saw a 10% rise to Rs 52,749 crore, while total wages in the wearing apparel rose 17% to Rs 40,888 crore.Core heavy industries and consumer segments also posted robust gains. Basic metals generated the highest absolute net profits among major groups at Rs 1.4 lakh crore (12.7% rise), while the wage bill crossed Rs 80,000 crore. Motor vehicles saw net profits climb 19% to Rs 1.2 lakh crore, with wage bill rising by nearly 12% to Rs 83,000 crore.
Article Summary: High-value segments, such as technology, heavy engineering and automotive, have led the profit growth in India's organised manufacturing sector in 2024-25. Despite headwinds, these sectors ensured resilient overall value addition and broader wage distribution across the formal manufacturing sector. Among industries, computer and electronic products recorded a 46% jump in profits to Rs 41,100 crore.

Article Title: Premium upgrades drive appliances' festive sales
Article Text:
Premium upgrades drive appliances' festive sales

NEW DELHI: India's festive appliance season exposed a divide in what shoppers were willing to pay for. Bigger televisions and higher-capacity appliances found buyers, while demand for some of the cheapest TV sets faded as Diwali approached. Several brands reported faster growth in sales value than in units, helped by both higher prices and a shift towards costlier models. Air conditioners were an exception at some companies, with more units sold as well as higher takings."Our premium television portfolio witnessed significant momentum, recording 600% growth this festive season, while our air purifier category recorded over 300% YoY growth this festive season," a Xiaomi India spokesperson said. The company did not disclose the volumes behind either figure.Hisense India sold 25% more units from Navratri to Dhanteras than in the same festive period last year, while sales value rose 35%. CEO Pankaj Rana said its TV business grew about 35% and ACs about 20%, without specifying whether those figures referred to units or value.At Thomson, early Navratri offers drew shoppers who had put off purchases, but sales momentum later weakened at the budget end.Avneet Singh Marwah, CEO of Super Plastronics, the Indian licensee for Thomson, Kodak and Blaupunkt, said higher input and freight costs had made buyers of entry-level sets more cautious. "In contrast, the premium segment witnessed robust growth of over 20%," he said, citing strong demand for 55-inch and 65-inch TVs.Intex Technologies reported a roughly 45% rise in festive sales value, with volume growth trailing. TVs, ACs and washing machines led the gains, with small appliances and speakers also contributing. Director Keshav Bansal said higher input costs and currency movements prompted price increases, while larger screens and higher-capacity appliances lifted the average bill. "Consumers were willing to spend more when they saw a meaningful difference in what the product offered," he said. Blue Star's room AC sales, meanwhile, rose more than 35% in both units and value.
Article Summary: India's festive appliance season exposed a divide in what shoppers were willing to pay for. Bigger televisions and higher-capacity appliances found buyers, while demand for some of the cheapest TV sets faded as Diwali approached. Several brands reported faster growth in sales value than in units.
