Article Title: Thiruvananthapuram holiday on November 11: Schools and state government offices to close for Beemapally Uroos
Article Text:
Kerala holiday update: Thiruvananthapuram declares local holiday for Beemapally Uroos, public exams to continue

Holiday applicable to schools and government offices

What is the Beemapally Uroos festival?

Beemapally Dargah's significance in Kerala

Thiruvananthapuram holiday November 11: The District Collector of Thiruvananthapuram has declared a local holiday for all educational institutions and state government offices within the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation limits on Wednesday, November 11, in connection with the annual Beemapally Uroos festival. The order applies to institutions and government offices operating within the corporation's jurisdiction.District Collector Anju K S announced the holiday as devotees prepare to participate in the annual festival at Beemapally Dargah Shareef. However, the district administration has clarified that public examinations scheduled in advance will take place according to the original timetable. The holiday declaration will not affect these examinations.The local holiday covers educational institutions and state government offices situated within the boundaries of the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation. The closure has been announced specifically in view of the Beemapally Uroos celebrations.Students appearing for pre-scheduled public examinations should note that the examinations will proceed without changes.The district administration has confirmed that the existing examination schedule will remain in force despite the holiday.The declaration is limited to the specified municipal corporation area. The order does not state that the holiday applies across the entire Thiruvananthapuram district.The Beemapally Uroos, also known as the Chandanakudam Mahotsavam, is a prominent annual religious festival held at the historic Beemapally Dargah Shareef in Thiruvananthapuram. The 10-day celebration attracts tens of thousands of devotees, pilgrims and visitors from different parts of Kerala and beyond.The festival commemorates the death anniversaries of Saint Sayyidhathunissa Beema Beevi and her son, Ashaikhu Sayidushaheed Maheen Aboobaker, who are buried at the shrine. According to local religious beliefs, both were descendants of the family of Prophet Muhammad.Beema Beevi and her son are remembered for their healing powers, spiritual teachings and commitment to social service. Their shrine has remained an important religious destination over several generations.Beemapally Dargah Shareef is regarded as a symbol of communal harmony in Kerala. The annual Uroos festival draws visitors from different religious communities and backgrounds, making it an important gathering in the region's religious and cultural calendar.The celebrations bring together devotees and tourists, with the shrine witnessing significant visitor participation during the 10-day festival.
Article Summary: Thiruvananthapuram declares local holiday for Beemapally Uroos, public exams to continue. The holiday covers educational institutions and state government offices. Public examinations scheduled in advance will take place according to original timetable. The 10-day celebration attracts tens of thousands of devotees, pilgrims and visitors.

Article Title: Russia's oil game runs dry as Ukrainian drones knock out 30% of refining capacity
Article Text:
Plumes of smoke rise from fires (centre) at an oil refinery following what the authorities say is a Ukrainian drone strike in the course of the Russia-Ukraine conflict, in Moscow

A series of Ukrainian drone attacks has knocked out a significant chunk of Russia's oil refining capacity, with operations affected at nine of the country's 35 major refineries over the past week. The strikes have reduced Russia's refining capacity by around 30% since late October, according to two industry sources. The attacks have affected facilities with a combined daily nameplate capacity of around 300,000 metric tonnes, or 2.2 million barrels.These include three major refineries in central Russia, as well as plants in Ryazan, Yaroslavl and the Volga region. Russia has a total primary refining capacity of approximately 930,000 tonnes per day.However, its refineries were processing around 700,000 tonnes, or five million barrels, of crude oil daily at the end of October. Industry sources estimate that the actual reduction in daily crude processing could reach 200,000 tonnes.The attacks have also added to Moscow's difficulties in tackling domestic fuel shortages while continuing to ship diesel to international markets under an export deal with US President Donald Trump.Ukraine intensified its strikes on Russian oil facilities after a proposed ceasefire on attacks against energy infrastructure, announced by Trump between Kyiv and Moscow in late October, failed to take effect.In the latest attack, on Wednesday, a Ukrainian drone hit the Kirishi oil refinery, Russia's second-largest, on Monday night. The strike triggered a fire at the facility and killed a woman, the governor of the Leningrad region said.Meanwhile, Russian forces continued targeting Ukraine's energy and transport infrastructure. Prime minister Sergii Koretskyi said on Wednesday that six large electricity substations across four central Ukrainian regions had been struck.In a post on Telegram, he also reported attacks on railway infrastructure in eastern and central Ukraine.The exchange of attacks has also drawn criticism from both sides over the proposed halt to strikes on energy facilities.Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov, in an article published in the daily newspaper Kommersant on Tuesday, said Ukraine was ignoring Trump's calls to stop attacks on Russian energy targets.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, however, said last week that Kyiv would continue striking targets linked to Russia's oil sector in retaliation for Moscow's attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.He said Ukrainian power plants, energy networks, heating systems and water supply systems were under constant attack, adding that Moscow had "refused the de-escalation steps that our partners talked about".
Article Summary: Strikes have reduced Russia's refining capacity by around 30% since late October. The attacks have affected facilities with a combined daily nameplate capacity of around 300,000 metric tonnes, or 2.2 million barrels. Russia has a total primary refining capacity of approximately 930,000 tonnes per day.

Article Title: ‘De-risk, not decouple’: Amid Nvidia controversy, Bessent says US-China must cooperate on AI risks despite rivalry
Article Text:
File photo: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent

US and China plan dialogue on superintelligence risks

Bessent outlines trade initiatives ahead of Trump-Xi meeting

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces shareholder lawsuit

The United States and China must work together to manage the risks posed by advanced artificial intelligence while recognising that their competition for technological leadership will continue, US treasury secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday.Bessent said the two countries should not underestimate their differences as they prepare to establish a new dialogue on “superintelligence” during US President Donald Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen next week.The meeting, scheduled on the sidelines of the November 18-19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ summit, will be Trump’s third meeting with Xi this year. Bessent, who is due to travel to China for the talks, said Washington wanted to build a relationship with Beijing based on “balance and reciprocity”.“As SI advances, so will the need to engage in new areas of risk management — and to demonstrate how two nations can reconcile the demands of competition with the responsibilities of leadership,” Bessent said in prepared remarks to the National Committee on US-China Relations in New York.He added that the two sides should “harbour no illusions about the differences between the United States and China”, noting that their interests and approaches would not always align.The proposed dialogue on superintelligence, or SI, is intended to help Washington and Beijing address shared risks and avoid misunderstandings between their respective systems, Bessent said.The discussions are expected to cover the evaluation and testing of advanced AI models before their release, as well as measures to ensure that human judgement remains in control of the technology.“We also expect to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release, and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology,” he said.The two countries have also agreed to establish a direct communication channel to alert each other about serious incidents involving the technology.Trump and Xi agreed on the AI alert system during their previous meeting at the White House in September. However, Trump had then expressed reluctance to introduce additional safeguards, saying he wanted to protect US leadership in the field, Reuters reported.Bessent also referred to trade agreements reached during the two previous Trump-Xi meetings, including plans for a “Board of Trade” to determine reciprocal tariff reductions on $30 billion worth of non-sensitive goods in each direction.China has also pledged to purchase US agricultural products, he said.A proposed “Board of Investment” would provide a structured forum to discuss market access for American companies operating in China and offer greater predictability for Chinese businesses, Bessent added.He acknowledged that the US trade deficit with China remained a point of friction but reiterated that Washington's objective was to reduce risks in the economic relationship rather than sever trade ties.“The US objective is to ‘de-risk, not to decouple’ from trade with China,” he said.Bessent invoked the first US trade voyage to China in 1784, when American merchants exchanged ginseng for Chinese tea, porcelain and silk, to underline the importance of maintaining areas of cooperation despite competing interests.Bessent did not refer in his remarks to the controversy surrounding Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, who is facing an internal investigation by the company's board over reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence services of having links to Chinese intelligence.China's foreign ministry has dismissed the espionage allegations as “groundless” and “a smear”. Nvidia has said its board has no reason to believe that US national security or the company's secrets were compromised, while Jensen Huang has pledged to cooperate with the internal review.The controversy has also prompted a shareholder lawsuit against Nvidia and its chief executive.According to news agency AP, retail investor Mark Kistenmacher filed a complaint in a California court on Monday, accusing the company and Huang of misleading investors about the relationship and its potential implications for national security and Nvidia's business.The complaint alleges that Nvidia failed to disclose Huang's relationship with Alice Huang and made misleading statements about its dealings with her company, Singapore-based Megaspeed International. The company had earlier said its compliance team had checked Megaspeed's activities and found no evidence of wrongdoing, AP reported.The lawsuit seeks unspecified damages and a jury trial on behalf of investors who purchased Nvidia shares between October 9, 2025, and November 8, 2026.Nvidia's independent directors said on Tuesday that they had appointed the New York-based law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a “thorough and independent investigation” into the matter. Joon H. Kim, a partner at the firm and a former acting US attorney for the Southern District of New York, will lead the inquiry.Trump said on Monday that the FBI was investigating the affair. He also said Huang had told him that he had no idea the woman could be involved in espionage, adding that he did not think the Nvidia chief had reason to worry.Nvidia shares fell 4.3% on Monday, wiping out around $190 billion in market value, and declined a further 5.5% by Tuesday's close.Huang has acknowledged the affair and apologised to his wife, family and the company in an open letter published on Nvidia's website.“I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security,” he said.
Article Summary: US and China plan dialogue on superintelligence risks. Bessent outlines trade initiatives ahead of Trump-Xi meeting. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces shareholder lawsuit over affair with businesswoman suspected by US intelligence services of having links to Chinese intelligence. China's foreign ministry has dismissed the espionage allegations as “groundless” and “a smear”

Article Title: Crude cools off: Oil prices hold near $90 per barrel as US-Iran war tensions ease
Article Text:
Crude oil price holds near $90 per barrel

Oil prices remained around the $90-per-barrel mark, with Brent crude futures trading at $92.29 per barrel, up 80 cents or 0.87%, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures rose 57 cents or 0.66% to $86.61 per barrel.Both benchmarks had settled at their lowest levels since August 31 for a second consecutive session.The decline comes as easing tensions between the US and Iran have reduced concerns over prolonged supply disruptions in the Middle East.Brent has shed around 17% in recent trading sessions, with Middle Eastern crude exports recovering to near pre-war levels. The recovery has also fuelled concerns about a potential supply glut, adding to the pressure on oil prices.Earlier on Monday, US President Donald Trump said that war with Iran was "militarily ... effectively over", signalling that he was not immediately considering a return to large-scale attacks."We're just keeping it the status quo," Trump told reporters during an appearance at the White House after meeting Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani.Trump said Iran had been "decapitated", but added that Washington was still seeking a long-term arrangement to ensure Tehran's nuclear programme was dismantled.Describing negotiations as showing "positive momentum", he said there was a "good chance" the conflict could end."They're talking to us, and they're talking very politely, And we'll see what happens," he said.He added that military action did not currently appear necessary, although US forces remained prepared to resume operations if circumstances changed."The military action doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing, but we're locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes," Trump said.Trump also said the US would maintain its naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now.Meanwhile, Middle Eastern crude exports have recovered close to pre-war levels, while OPEC production increased in October, led by Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq, according to a Reuters survey. However, export constraints, depleted global inventories and disrupted fuel shipments continue to pose challenges. Industry leaders have warned that rebuilding oil stocks could take up to two years.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures trading at $92.29 per barrel, up 80 cents or 0.87%. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures rose 57 cents or0.66% to $86.61 per barrel. Both benchmarks had settled at their lowest levels since August 31 for a second consecutive session.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $1 trillion IPO valuation, plans nearly $90 billion fundraising
Article Text:
Anthropic is targeting a $1 trillion valuation through its upcoming IPO alongside a private placement, intending to issue 825 million shares at a price range of $70 to $78 each.

Anthropic is targeting a $1 trillion valuation in what could become one of the biggest IPOs in history, with plans to raise nearly $90 billion through a public offering and a separate private placement backed by seven major technology companies.The Claude maker has also reported an $81 billion revenue run-rate, putting its growth, valuation and massive AI infrastructure commitments under the spotlight.According to Reuters, the proposed IPO will involve the sale of 825 million shares, including 801.35 million new Class A shares issued by Anthropic and another 23.65 million shares sold by existing shareholders.At the estimated price of $70 to $78 per share, the public offering could raise between $57.75 billion and $64.35 billion.A separate $26 billion private placement would take the combined fundraising to approximately $90.35 billion, making it one of the largest capital-raising exercises in the technology industry.The private placement will bring seven major technology companies into the fundraising exercise, with AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC agreeing to purchase $26 billion worth of Anthropic's Class N common stock.The participation of these companies underlines the growing financial and strategic links between AI developers and the semiconductor industry.Separately, Anthropic's board members and affiliates have indicated interest in purchasing up to $303 million worth of Class A shares at the IPO offering price.Anthropic's rapid revenue growth is another major factor behind its ambitious valuation target. The company said its run-rate revenue stood at approximately $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, marking an increase of $10 billion from September 30.The figure reflects an annualised estimate based on its current revenue pace rather than actual earnings over a 12-month period, highlighting the pace at which demand for its AI products is expanding.
Article Summary: Anthropic is targeting a $1 trillion valuation in what could become one of the biggest IPOs in history. Plans to raise nearly $90 billion through a public offering and a separate private placement backed by seven major technology companies. The AI maker has also reported an $81 billion revenue run-rate, putting its growth and massive AI infrastructure commitments under the spotlight.

Article Title: Asian stocks today: Markets rally as Wall Street rebounds, oil prices ease on Iran de-escalation hopes
Article Text:
Asian stocks opened higher on Tuesdayfollowing gains in US equities

Wall Street rebound and easing oil prices lift sentiment

Nvidia shares remain under pressure, US inflation data in focus

Asian stocks advanced on Tuesday, extending a recovery in global markets after Wall Street recorded its strongest single-day gain since April. A decline in oil prices following US President Donald Trump's decision to hold off on fresh military strikes against Iran also lifted investor sentiment.Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 2.6% to 60,279.37, while South Korea's Kospi climbed 4% to 5,219.37.Taiwan's Taiex gained 3.4%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng advanced 0.4% to 24,535.74, and the Shanghai Composite edged 0.4% higher to 3,673.54.Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 1.1% to 9,131.70. Meanwhile, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 1.5% in early trading, according to Reuters.Technology stocks led gains across several markets. Shares in SoftBank Group, an investor in OpenAI, jumped 15% ahead of its earnings announcement. Tokyo Electron rose 5.6%, while Advantest gained 3.4%.In South Korea, Samsung Electronics climbed 4.6% and SK Hynix advanced 5.6%. AFP also reported gains in Taiwan's technology sector, with chipmaker TSMC rising more than 1% and MediaTek gaining over 7%.The rally in Asia followed a strong session on Wall Street on Monday. The S&P 500 jumped 2.3% for a second consecutive gain, leaving it 3.4% below its record high set last month.The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 2.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 2.7%.US stocks had suffered a sharp sell-off last week after Democratic victories in the midterm elections raised concerns that governments could impose restrictions on the expansion of AI data centres.Investors were also worried about the high cost of building the infrastructure and whether companies would generate sufficient returns on their investments.The fall in oil prices provided further support to equities by easing inflation concerns. Brent crude, the international benchmark, was down around 0.9% to $91.74 a barrel in early Asian trading, while US benchmark crude fell 1% to $85.97.Oil prices have declined after Trump said he would hold off on new military strikes against Iran for the time being. He has also indicated that a resumption of fighting was “highly unlikely” if Washington saw progress in negotiations to end the conflict.Trump said on Monday there was “positive momentum” towards ending the war after meeting Qatar's prime minister at the White House. He also maintained that the US remained “locked and loaded”, while saying further strikes were unlikely given the preference of key Gulf allies for maintaining the status quo.However, Reuters quoted Nick Twidale, chief market strategist at ATFX Global, as saying that a considerable gap remained between diplomatic efforts and a lasting peace agreement.“The risk now is that markets have moved too far, too quickly ... any indication that negotiations are faltering could see a substantial rebound in prices as traders rapidly rebuild the geopolitical risk premium,” he said.Despite the broader technology-led recovery, Nvidia shares fell around 4.3% on Monday, extending pressure on the company amid reports about its chief executive Jensen Huang.The chipmaker said its board was investigating whether Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence operation. The allegations centred on his reported relationship with a Chinese business executive. Nvidia's board said it had “no reason to believe” that national security or company secrets had been compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information.China's foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun dismissed the allegations as “nothing but smears against China”, according to AP.Investors are also watching earnings reports from technology companies this week, including AI cloud computing firm CoreWeave, as concerns persist over the cost and profitability of the AI infrastructure boom. Nvidia is due to report its results next week.Attention was also turning to US inflation data due later on Tuesday, which could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions. Economists polled by Reuters expect consumer prices to have risen 0.3% in October, while core inflation is forecast to increase 0.2%.Traders were pricing in an 84% chance of an interest rate hike next month, up from 74% a week earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool cited by Reuters.In currency markets, the US dollar rose to 158.06 Japanese yen from 157.90 yen, while the euro slipped to $1.1222 from $1.1266.
Article Summary: Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 2.6% to 60,279.37, while South Korea's Kospi climbed 4% to 5,219.37. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 1.5% in early trading. Technology stocks led gains across several markets.

Article Title: $69.3 billion IPO? Anthropic shares price details with banks, then retracts
Article Text:
Anthropic is planning its market debut under symbol "ANT"

Anthropic's proposed initial public offering (IPO), which could have raised nearly $70 billion, was briefly outlined in a securities filing circulated to banks before the artificial intelligence company retracted the pricing details.An Anthropic representative sent bankers a copy of a filing showing plans to offer around 867 million shares at a price range of $70 to $80 apiece. The company subsequently sent another email saying the pricing information was inaccurate and that an updated filing would follow, reported Reuters.Anthropic did not specify which details were incorrect as there has been no public confirmation around this.The original email, cited by Reuters, indicated that the proposed offering would involve 866.7 million Class A shares, including around 843.3 million shares sold by Anthropic and 23.3 million shares offered by existing shareholders. At the top of the proposed price range, the IPO could have raised $69.3 billion.The original filing also showed that Anthropic had lined up a separate private placement worth $26 billion, involving some of the world's biggest technology companies. Alphabet's Google, Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) had agreed to participate by purchasing Anthropic's Class N common stock at the IPO price.The private placement was to close immediately after the public offering.Anthropic is expected to formally launch its IPO roadshow on Tuesday, with pricing expected the following week.The proposed listing comes as Anthropic seeks to capitalise on growing demand for generative AI and its Claude family of models. Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives, including chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, the company has emerged as one of the leading players in the AI industry.In its IPO disclosures, Anthropic said it planned to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. However, the number of shares to be offered and the price range had not been finalised, based on public information.Anthropic reported revenue of $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, alongside a net loss of $80.7 billion. A substantial portion of the reported loss was linked to changes in the fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and other financing instruments, rather than being a direct measure of operating cash expenditure.The company expects significant spending to continue as it invests in computing infrastructure, research, AI safety and expansion. Its disclosures also warn that it may not achieve or sustain profitability.The filing outlined risks associated with the development of advanced AI systems, including the possibility that they could pose catastrophic or existential threats to humanity without adequate safeguards and oversight. It also highlighted risks arising from misuse, autonomous capabilities and the possibility that AI research could advance faster than the ability to evaluate and secure new models.Anthropic's IPO comes amid growing scrutiny of the enormous capital requirements of the AI industry. Several companies in the AI infrastructure and data centre sectors have delayed or withdrawn planned listings, while concerns over interest rates and the sustainability of AI spending have weighed on companies such as CoreWeave.Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion for Anthropic, although expectations have since moderated, with $1.5 trillion viewed as the upper end of the range, Reuters had reported.The company's growth has been supported by major technology partners, particularly Google and Amazon, which are also investors, computing infrastructure providers and distribution partners. Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including the two companies, highlighting its dependence on substantial future infrastructure capacity.
Article Summary: Anthropic sent bankers a copy of a filing showing plans to offer around 867 million shares at a price range of $70 to $80 apiece. The company subsequently sent another email saying the pricing information was inaccurate. At the top of the proposed price range, the IPO could have raised $69.3 billion.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang loses $7.4 billion in 30 minutes, drops 2 spots in Forbes rich list
Article Text:
The investigation follows a report by The New York Times last month that US intelligence agencies had identified a close relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen suspected by Washington of gathering information for Beijing.

Allegation against Alice Huang

A photo shows NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang with a woman confirmed by a Reuters source to be Alice Huang in Taipei, Taiwan released on June 7, 2024.

Trump defends Nvidia chief

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife Lori Huang attend the 12th Breakthrough Prize ceremony gala in Santa Monica, California, US on April 18

What lies ahead for Nvidia

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang slipped to 10th place on Forbes’ list of the world’s richest people after his net worth plunged by $7.4 billion on Monday. The drop followed a sharp fall in the company’s share price amid an investigation into his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.Huang’s net worth dropped from $162.2 billion to $154.7 billion within the first half-hour of trading, pushing him down two places from number 8 to number 10 in the Forbes real-time billionaire rankings, according to a report by Forbes. He briefly fell out of the top 10 after Nvidia shares opened more than 7 per cent lower, wiping out $10.3 billion from his fortune.Also Read | Nvidia's billionaire boss has admitted to cheating on his wife. Was he the target of Chinese spying? Nvidia shares were down 5.5 per cent at 1.30pm EST, after falling as much as 7 per cent in premarket trading. This was the first trading session since the company confirmed an investigation into Huang. The development also put him below Berkshire Hathaway chairman Warren Buffett and Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison in the billionaire rankings.The fall in Nvidia shares also hit the company's market value. Its market capitalisation dropped from $4.5 trillion. Nvidia has frequently competed with Apple for the position of the world's most valuable publicly traded company.The share price decline followed Huang's admission on Sunday that he had an affair. In a statement to employees, he apologised for his actions and said he supported the company's investigation.Nvidia's board said it had appointed a committee of independent directors, along with external legal counsel, to examine all available information. However, it added that it had "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised."The investigation follows a report by The New York Times last month that US intelligence agencies had identified a close relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen suspected by Washington of gathering information for Beijing.According to The New York Times, Alice Huang was recruited by Beijing's top spy agency to collect information on Jensen Huang for China's ministry of state security. The report cited a memo circulated within the Trump administration.It remains unclear when the two first met. However, they were photographed together at a bar in June 2024.Alice Huang has also reportedly had connections with other artificial intelligence chip industry leaders, including executives at Gigabyte, a company that assembles Nvidia supercomputers.She has described herself as the chief executive of Singapore-based neocloud and AI computing services provider Megaspeed. However, the company removed her as managing director from its official paperwork after the first eight months, according to The New York Times.Megaspeed was established in 2023 after Chinese gaming and cloud computing company 7Road spun off its overseas operations in Singapore. The company partners with Nvidia and supplies its technology across the Asia-Pacific region.US authorities have been investigating the company's possible role in China's access to Nvidia chips since 2024. A Commerce Department official had found Nvidia equipment still packed in boxes at a data centre site in Malaysia, raising concerns that it could be shipped elsewhere.Also Read| What Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang first told the world about Alice Huang, the woman he has admitted having an affair with US intelligence officials had briefed President Donald Trump about their findings concerning Alice Huang around a year ago, The New York Times reported. However, Trump did not take action at the time.An Nvidia spokesperson had earlier told the newspaper that "Jensen’s interactions with Ms Huang are not unusual or unexpected," adding that meeting customers was part of his job.Huang has also emerged as an ally and technology adviser to Trump. The US president rolled back restrictions introduced by the Biden administration in 2022 to limit global exports of advanced AI chips.Trump defended the Nvidia chief on Sunday night, calling him an "honorable guy". He also said he would still include Huang in his upcoming visit to China.The investigation comes at a crucial time for Nvidia, which is scheduled to announce its quarterly earnings next Tuesday after the market closes.The company's second-quarter results showed its data centre business generating $89 billion in revenue, up 117 per cent year-on-year. The segment accounted for around 92 per cent of Nvidia's total revenue for the quarter, while overall revenue stood at $96.2 billion, beating expectations.Nvidia was also the only company among the so-called Magnificent Seven, a group comprising Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Meta and Tesla, to record a premarket decline on Monday.
Article Summary: Huang’s net worth dropped from $162.2 billion to $154.7 billion within the first half-hour of trading, pushing him down two places from number 8 to number 10 in the Forbes real-time billionaire rankings. He briefly fell out of the top 10 after Nvidia shares opened more than 7 per cent lower, wiping out $10.3 billion from his fortune. The share price decline followed Huang's admission on Sunday that he had an affair.

Article Title: Asean's $7.1 trillion infrastructure ambition hit by massive funding gap: ADB
Article Text:
By 2040, Southeast Asia will require an astounding $7.1 trillion for infrastructure improvements, with reports indicating a $4 trillion funding shortage.

The report highlighted the following key findings:

Prioritising essential infrastructure: Governments should focus on projects that strengthen transportation networks, electricity supply and healthcare facilities, the bank said.

Governments should focus on projects that strengthen transportation networks, electricity supply and healthcare facilities, the bank said. Southeast Asian economies will require an estimated $7.1 trillion in infrastructure investments by 2040, but the region is facing a substantial funding shortfall, according to a new report released by the asian development bank (ADB) on Tuesday.According to news agency Reuters, the ADB has revised its assessment of infrastructure requirements for the association of southeast asian nations (ASEAN), more than doubling its earlier estimate of $3.15 trillion for the 2016-2030 period.

Article Title: Nvidia, Jensen Huang sued over alleged Chinese spy links, shareholder fraud claims
Article Text:
Nvidia, CEO Jensen Huang sued over alleged ties to suspected Chinese spy, shareholder fraud claims

Nvidia and its Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang have been sued in a proposed class-action lawsuit accusing them of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's alleged ties to a suspected Chinese spy, according to a court filing cited by Reuters.The lawsuit comes as Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation involving Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed.US authorities reportedly suspect that Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information about the Nvidia chief and the company.The allegations have also drawn scrutiny to Megaspeed, which purchases Nvidia's artificial intelligence chips and has been investigated over suspicions that it helped Beijing gain access to advanced processors restricted from export to China.China has rejected allegations of involvement in an espionage operation targeting Huang, describing the claims as baseless."The narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said during a media briefing, as quoted by AFP.Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe that US national security or the company's confidential information had been compromised, but would examine all available information as part of its investigation. Huang has backed the probe and agreed to cooperate.The developments also follow Huang's recent admission in a message to Nvidia employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife. He apologised to his family and colleagues but did not identify the woman involved.
Article Summary: N Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang sued over alleged ties to suspected Chinese spy, shareholder fraud claims. Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. China has rejected allegations of involvement in an espionage operation targeting Huang, describing the claims as baseless.

Article Title: ‘Will have to return deposits’: Musk says Tesla will end Cybertruck production, rejects unprofitability claims
Article Text:
Elon Musk pulling the plug on Tesla's Cybertruck

Tesla will have to refund deposits to a large number of customers who placed orders for its Cybertruck pickup, as demand has outstripped the company's production capacity, CEO Elon Musk said. The electric vehicle maker plans to wind down production of the model at its Texas factory in about eight months to make room for its autonomous Cybercab.“We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people,” Musk said in a post on X on Monday, acknowledging that the Cybertruck's order rate was significantly higher than its production rate.Further rejecting unprofitability rumours, he added, "This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media, but rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production."The latest comments follow Musk's announcement last week that Tesla would add an extra production shift to clear outstanding Cybertruck orders before ending production.The manufacturing line is expected to be shut down around mid-2027, with resources redirected towards scaling up Cybercab output.Musk has rejected suggestions that the decision to discontinue the pickup was driven by profitability concerns. He argued that the complexity of manufacturing the Cybertruck made expanding its production less valuable than using the capacity to build more Cybercabs.“This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media, but rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production,” he said.Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and began customer deliveries in November 2023. Despite Musk's ambitious sales projections, the pickup has struggled to attract the expected demand. US sales fell 48 per cent to 20,237 units last year, according to Kelley Blue Book, far below Musk's earlier projection of annual sales reaching 250,000 vehicles.The Cybercab, unveiled in October 2024, is a two-seater autonomous electric vehicle designed without a steering wheel or pedals. It is central to Musk's plan to build a robotaxi network and expand Tesla's self-driving ambitions.
Article Summary: Tesla will have to refund deposits to a large number of customers who placed orders for its Cybertruck pickup, CEO Elon Musk said. The electric vehicle maker plans to wind down production of the model at its Texas factory in about eight months to make room for its autonomous Cybercab.

Article Title: Nvidia shares drop after CEO Jensen Huang admits affair with suspected Chinese spy; what it means for company
Article Text:
Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife but did not provide details about the relationship.

Jensen Huang & the 'Chinese spy' scandal

Impact on Nvidia and its shares

Nvidia shares declined in after-hours trading on Monday following the announcement of an internal investigation to find out if the company’s chief executive Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The investigation has raised questions about Jensen Huang’s future at the AI chipmaker which is among the most valuable listed companies in the world.Announced on Sunday, the investigation has drawn attention to Huang's position at Nvidia, the world's most valuable chipmaker. His future is also under scrutiny because of his prominent role as one of the leading salesmen of the artificial intelligence boom.Jensen Huang, 63, has headed Nvidia since he established the company in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. His long tenure makes him one of Silicon Valley's longest-serving chief executives among company founders.Born in Taiwan and brought up in the US, Huang emerged as a key figure in the artificial intelligence revolution. He steered Nvidia from its original business of manufacturing graphics chips for video games to becoming the world's leading supplier of AI processors.The company launched the internal inquiry following a media report alleging that Huang had a close association with a Chinese businesswoman who had allegedly shared information with Beijing.In a message to Nvidia employees, Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife but did not provide details about the relationship.The New York Times reported last month that Huang had been involved in a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is not related to him. US authorities investigated Alice Huang and concluded that she was an asset of Chinese intelligence.Megaspeed's website identifies the company as an Nvidia Cloud Partner in the Asia-Pacific region. It also lists Nvidia's GB200 NVL72 and HGX H100 chips among the products it offers.The developments also had repercussions in South Korea. Madison Huang, Jensen Huang's daughter and an Nvidia executive, called off a scheduled visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference due to begin on Monday, according to companies that had been due to meet her.Madison Huang had been scheduled to visit South Korean artificial intelligence startup Rebellions and participate in a question-and-answer session with Kakao Mobility. Rebellions said both engagements had been called off because of "unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia."South Korean media reported that Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day conference expected to attract around 2,000 participants, would go ahead as scheduled. The event is set to focus on physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.According to a Reuters report, trading in perpetual futures on the Hyperliquid exchange, along with after-hours share transactions on the Blue Ocean system, indicated that Nvidia shares were changing hands at around $178.60. This is a decline of more than 4% from the stock's closing price of $186.64 on the Nasdaq on Friday.Nvidia's chip technology has played a central role in several major shifts in the technology industry, spanning video gaming, autonomous vehicles, cloud computing and artificial intelligence.Huang's early decision to invest in AI proved significant. By the time ChatGPT was launched in late 2022, Nvidia's processors were already central to the computing infrastructure needed to meet the rapidly growing demand for AI applications.The company's market value has since climbed sharply, making it one of the world's most valuable businesses and an essential supplier to leading technology companies. Nvidia's valuation rose from $420 billion in late 2022 to $4.5 trillion as of November 6."The market's probably telling you now this does no favours ⁠to the stock whatsoever in a time when there's a lot of conjecture as to the build out of data centres," Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne told Reuters.However, Weston said he did not expect Huang, whom he described as the "godfather of AI", to be replaced."If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down — it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest,” he said.The scrutiny of Huang's relationship with Alice Huang has emerged at a sensitive point for Nvidia. Investors are already questioning whether the AI boom that fuelled the company's extraordinary growth can be sustained. The board's investigation has added another layer of uncertainty by raising questions about the future of the executive most closely linked to Nvidia's success.The issue has also drawn attention from senior Republicans in the US House of Representatives, who have sought briefings from Huang following The New York Times report, pointing to concerns over national security.Nvidia has maintained that its board has "no reason to believe" that US national security or company secrets were compromised. However, an independent committee of directors will examine all the information available as part of its review.Analysts cautioned that an extended investigation or internal review could affect Nvidia's investment decisions and product launches, potentially creating wider repercussions for the semiconductor industry.Ryu Young-ho, a senior analyst at NH Investment & Securities, said competitors such as Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) could receive increased attention in the near term. This could also bring Samsung into greater focus because of its close business ties ⁠with AMD.However, Ryu said Nvidia's products would be difficult to replace, which could limit the overall impact of the developments. He added that shipments to China might face further delays, depending on how the situation unfolded.South Korea's deputy science minister said on Monday that the government did not expect any disruption to deliveries of Nvidia graphics processing units covered by existing contracts, despite the challenges currently confronting the company.Shares of Nvidia's major Asian chip suppliers recovered on Monday following last week's selloff in AI-related stocks. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) rose 6.5%, while Samsung Electronics gained 2.9% and SK Hynix advanced 4.7%.Several prominent personalities also commented on Huang's admission. Billionaire investor Bill Ackman, who founded Pershing Square Capital Management, described the Nvidia chief executive as an "incredible human" in a post on X. However, he added that ‌if "indeed this is ⁠more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem.""I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security," he added.Tesla CEO Elon Musk responded with "I agree" to a post by Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire. Maguire had said Huang "did something incredibly dumb" that was "bad for America", while also maintaining that "Jensen is irreplaceable for America's AI leadership".US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he had not discussed the allegations with Huang. He nevertheless described the Nvidia CEO as a fine person. "I hope everything's fine. He's done such an incredible job," he added.Asked whether he believed he should have acted on the intelligence after being briefed about it, Trump said: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for ⁠it. You have to hear it."The New York Times reported that Trump had been briefed on the intelligence findings approximately a year ago but decided against taking action based on the information.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife but did not provide details about the relationship. The New York Times reported last month that Huang had been involved in a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed. US authorities investigated Alice Huang and concluded that she was an asset of Chinese intelligence.

Article Title: 1.14 lakh startups generate more than 12 lakh jobs in India: Finance ministry
Article Text:
Finance Ministry

NEW DELHI: More than 1.14 lakh startups in India have created over 12 lakh jobs so far, the finance ministry said in its latest review of the Indian economy.In the report titled, ‘The Indian Economy: A Review January 2024’, the Department of Economic Affairs said that the 1.14 lakh startups recognised by the government under the 'Startup India initiative’ created more than 12 lakh jobs (as of October 2023).The state-owned e-commerce platform Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) clocked more than 63 lakh transactions till November 2023, the document read.Despite facing global challenges in 2023 like valuation issues, few IPOs, regulatory changes and macroeconomic and geopolitical trends, India remains the third largest tech start-up ecosystem globally, with over 950 tech startups founded last year.The cumulative funding for more than 31,000 tech start ups has exceeded $70 billion (from 2019 to 2023), according to a recent report by Nasscom in collaboration with Zinnov.“In 2023, despite facing global economic and regulatory challenges, Indian tech startups have prioritised the imperative of enhancing their business fundamentals, driving profitability and growth,” said Debjani Ghosh, President, Nasscom.“The proliferation of tech startups in tier 2 and 3 cities marks the ecosystem's resilience,” she added.Navigating 2024, tech startup founders expect to continue the revenue growth path with measured steps focusing on optimising expenditure and maximising profitability for B2B tech startups.Investments in deeptech will continue an upward trend in 2024. With generative AI (GenAI) acceleration, 70 per cent of start-up founders are embedding artificial intelligence (AI) in their solutions.As funding becomes scarce for the Indian startup ecosystem in general, the explosion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has given a new lease of life to entrepreneurs and founders in the country, as the Centre extends support to the sector.
Article Summary: The state-owned e-commerce platform Open Network for Digital Commerce clocked more than 63 lakh transactions till November 2023. India remains the third largest tech start-up ecosystem globally, with over 950 tech startups founded last year. The cumulative funding for more than 31,000 tech start ups has exceeded $70 billion.

Article Title: Startups Revolutionizing Carbon Dioxide into Valuable Products
Article Text: For most perfume makers, ingredients to make it smell great are the most important feature. But for Stafford Sheehan, a cofounder and chemist at Air Company, the most important part of perfume-making has no scent at all.New York-based Air Company uses technology that converts planet-warming carbon dioxide into ethanol, which is then blended with essential oils and water to produce perfume. While the pale yellow-color Air Eau de Parfum is about 50% more expensive than Coco Chanel’s signature No. 5, Sheehan says his product is uniquely valuable: Every 50-milliliter bottle uses 3.6 grams of CO2 that otherwise would have been released into the atmosphere. Its package reads: “Turning CO2 into something beautiful.”While the volume of CO2 utilized in the bottle is extremely small, Air Company’s perfume showcases one way the coming wave of captured carbon can be put to use. Renewable energy and electric cars alone won’t be enough to cut CO2 emissions to zero. The world will almost certainly need to capture billions of tons of the gas annually in the coming decades. Large amounts will likely be stored underground.Using it — so-called carbon capture and utilization, or CCU — to create new products from perfume to jet fuel could be an important tool in the fight against climate change, too, though the nascent industry has major hurdles to overcome.Roughly 230 million tons of CO2 are utilized every year, according to a 2019 report by the International Energy Agency. While roughly one-third of that is reused to force more oil from the ground — hardly a carbon-neutral process — CCU advocates say that the number of companies coming up with new uses for carbon has mushroomed in recent years, paving a way to unlock climate benefits. Carbon-derived fuels and chemicals, for example, could theoretically grow to the scale of billions of tons of CO2 use per year if companies could perfect their technology and lower costs.Calgary-based CleanO2 transforms CO2 captured from building heating boilers into feedstock to make soap. Newlight Technologies, a biotechnology startup based in California, takes carbon pulled directly from the air and turns it into biodegradable plastics. Germany’s Covestro AG, one of the world’s largest polymer manufacturers, is also switching some of its fossil fuel-based feedstocks to carbon-derived materials for everything ranging from car shells to medical devices and stadium roofs.Most companies working on CO2-sequestering products are still in their infancy. To grow the emerging sector, global venture capitalists in 2022 poured nearly $500 million into carbon utilization businesses, according to the IEA. That’s in stark contrast to 2015, when barely any venture money went to technologies that utilize CO2.“It’s just a whole different landscape today than it was a decade ago,” says Sasha Mackler, executive director of the energy program at Washington, DC-based non-profit Bipartisan Policy Center.Jennifer Holmgren, chief executive officer of LanzaTech Global Inc., has experienced the shifting sentiment firsthand. The Illinois-based company uses a carbon-eating bacteria – discovered in the guts of rabbits and preserved as powder – to make alternative ethanol in bioreactors not dissimilar to how breweries ferment beer. In the early 2010s, when Holmgren touted carbon-derived ethanol to prospective customers, her sales pitch was met with skepticism.But the tide began turning later that decade. In 2018, the company’s jet fuel produced from the emissions of a Chinese steel mill helped power a Transatlantic flight. LanzaTech has also inked agreements with airlines including Japan’s All Nippon Airways to supply CO2-derived jet fuel. And LanzaJet, the company’s spin-off, plans to start producing sustainable jet fuels at a commercial scale this year.Yet for all the hype around sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) using captured carbon, the industry is still an extremely small player. Almost every major airline in the world has pledged to use at least 10% sustainable jet fuels by 2030, yet SAF makes up only 0.1% of global aviation fuel supply — and much of it is made from sources other than captured CO2, such as used cooking oil.“There’s a lot more interest because consumers have become much more interested in buying things that are lower carbon,” says Holmgren. That’s enabled LanzaTech to expand the number of products that utilize CO2.American plastic container maker Plastipak, for instance, has partnered with LanzaTech to produce carbon-derived packaging materials, while polyester converted from LanzaTech’s ethanol has replaced its petroleum-based counterpart at a pilot scale in Lululemon shorts, Zara dresses, H&M yoga pants, On running shoes and Craghoppers jackets. Like SAF, though, there’s still a long way to go for CO2-derived polyester to reach meaningful levels of use.Momentum to grow beyond one-off products and low-scale production has also been supercharged by a growing array of regulations and incentives around the world. For instance, the Inflation Reduction Act that US President Joe Biden signed in 2022 raised the tax credit for carbon capture and utilization by more than 70% to $60 per metric ton in an effort to make costly projects more financially appealing.To keep the climate within habitable limits, the IEA estimates that carbon capture will have to grow to 7.6 billion tons of CO2 annually by mid-century. CCU will play a role, though just how big remains to be seen. Not every use case is created equal and some approaches, such as dissolving compressed CO2 in water to make carbonated beverages, only store the gas temporarily. To quantify the true climate benefit of carbon utilization, experts say third-party verification is badly needed.The rise of CCU technology comes as another key approach in President Biden’s net-zero roadmap is hitting a bit of a wall. Carbon capture and storage — that is, gathering CO2 as it’s released from a coal-fired power plant or other emissions source and sequestering it underground — has faced challenges because carbon is often captured in one place and stored in another. That requires pipelines to transport the gas, which many local communities have opposed. Blackrock-backed Navigator, for example, recently announced it was scrapping a planned 1,300-mile CO2 pipeline.Carbon utilization companies say that they can sidestep that issue by using carbon near or at where it’s captured.At its 12-acre factory in Brooklyn, Glenwood Mason Supply demonstrates how. The concrete manufacturer takes CO2 captured at a residential building by its partner company, CarbonQuest, and uses a technique licensed from low-carbon concrete startup CarbonCure to convert the compressed carbon into a powder not unlike dry ice. It then injects it into industrial mixers. There, the CO2 meets cement, sand and aggregate, setting off a series of chemical reactions. The final result is concrete blocks with CO2 sealed in.The technique not only stores carbon but it can also make the blocks marginally stronger. The company estimates that it has utilized about 100 tons of CO2 in total since 2020. Even if the blocks break down, the stored carbon won’t be released as CO2 because it’s been mineralized.“Cement is a big offender in carbon emissions,” says Constance Cincotta, founder of the concrete factory. She became intrigued by the technology and its ability to lower her company's climate impact after hearing about it at an industry conference in the early 2010s. But it wasn't until CarbonCure came on the scene a few years ago that the prospect of CO2-storing cement became tangible. Glenwood Mason then sourced CO2 locally from CarbonQuest, which captures carbon from buildings in New York. Those factors have enabled large-scale production.While Cincotta’s intended to help the planet, she and her team discovered that sinking CO2 into concrete blocks is good for the business, too. In 2019, New York City — where the majority of the company’s concrete blocks are sold — passed a regulation requiring all buildings to shrink their carbon footprint 40% by the end of the decade. Glenwood Mason’s phones have been ringing ever since, with calls from architects and property developers who want to leverage their lower-carbon building materials to cut emissions, says Jeff Hansen, the company’s vice president in architectural sales and marketing.The factory’s CO2-storing concrete blocks also caught the eye of Amazon.com Inc, which in 2022 persuaded a real estate developer to purchase roughly 50,000 blocks for the construction of a new warehouse in New York that Amazon has leased. Had Glenwood Mason not sealed CO2 in its blocks, it wouldn’t have won the contract, Hansen says. To figure out how to pack more carbon into its products, the company has set up a laboratory in its factory to test the reaction between CO2 and other concrete feedstocks under different temperatures and humidity levels.But figuring out the right formula is only one consideration. Utilizing CO2 often comes with an additional cost. As the demand for CO2-derived products climbs, that green premium is expected to go down. Yet “it’s very hard to be a cost parity with a 100-year-old industry that doesn’t even have to pay for its externalities,” says Holmgren of LanzaTech. Even with economies of scale, Holmgren estimates that carbon-containing fabrics will still likely cost as much as 20% higher than conventional ones.“It’s unlikely that we will ever be a cost parity,” she says.In addition to the cost barrier, CCU companies also have to convince end users that may be suspicious of unproven new technologies.Changing feedstocks “does come with risks,” says Keith Wiggins, chief executive officer of Econic Technologies, a British startup that specializes in making carbon-derived chemicals. To get risk-averse industries onboard, Wiggins says his company is laser-focused on those that are under consumer pressure to change course.That strategy seems to be working. Econic has teamed up with three manufacturers in the US, China and India to produce mattresses, outdoor garments and building insulation materials that utilize CO2. The first batch of products using the company’s technology are scheduled to enter the market in 2024.For all the promise of the carbon utilization industry, it remains to be seen if it can challenge the status quo. While Air Company started selling carbon-derived perfume in 2021, the startup has yet to build its first commercial plant, Sheehan says, citing the time-consuming process needed for collecting data and fine-tuning the technology for large-scale production.Fow now, the company’s demonstration facility in New York City — where CO2 and hydrogen gas flow through tubes into a reactor to form chemical reactions, aided by catalysts made from a confidential mixture of metals — is designed to yield at least 10,000 gallons of CO2-derived liquid annually. The limited production capacity has left many orders for its perfume — as well as jet fuels and Air Vodka, another popular product made from CO2 — unfilled.“We need to scale these facilities to the size of oil refineries today in order to have the impact on climate change that we want to have,” Sheehan says.
Article Summary: New York-based Air Company uses technology that converts planet-warming carbon dioxide into ethanol, which is then blended with essential oils and water to produce perfume. Carbon-derived fuels and chemicals, for example, could theoretically grow to the scale of billions of tons of CO2 use per year if companies could perfect their technology.

Article Title: E-commerce firm Udaan raises $340 million ahead of planned IPO
Article Text: Indian e-commerce firm Udaan raised $340 million to strengthen its supply chain and boost vendor partnerships ahead of a stock market debut planned for 2025.The Series E round was done via a combination of fresh equity and conversion of debt, the Bangalore-based company said in a statement Thursday. The round was led by M&G Plc and existing investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners and DST Global participated.The round “fully funds our business plan,” Vaibhav Gupta, Udaan co-founder and chief executive officer, said in the statement. “It enables our continued journey of growth and profitability, positioning us well to be public-market ready in the next 12-18 months.”Udaan, which competes with Reliance Industries Ltd. and Walmart Inc.’s Flipkart in helping smaller merchants source their goods, runs an online marketplace and logistics networks that help mum-and-pop stores get quicker deliveries and cut traditional middlemen out. That kind of digital-led wholesale business, though a very small part of India’s overall retail market, is expected to swell to $150 billion in sales in a decade, according to McKinsey & Co.The startup targets an initial public offering in 2025, though it’s yet to decide whether it will do so in India or overseas, Gupta told Bloomberg News last month.Udaan was founded in 2016 by three engineers who previously worked at Flipkart. The trio together ran the company until Gupta, one of the founders, took over as CEO in 2021. The other two founders — Amod Malviya and Sujeet Kumar — are board members.
Article Summary: Indian e-commerce firm Udaan raised $340 million to strengthen its supply chain. The Series E round was done via a combination of fresh equity and conversion of debt. The startup targets an initial public offering in 2025, though it’s yet to decide whether it will do so in India or overseas.

Article Title: Minuscule AI startup raises $41 million to tap India growth
Article Text: A generative artificial intelligence startup targeting the Indian market raised $41 million in fresh funding, the largest such round by an early-stage AI contender in the country.Sarvam AI is building large language models targeted at unique uses in Indian languages at price points that the country’s 1.4 billion people can afford. The Series A funding round was led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, and participants included Silicon Valley billionaire Vinod Khosla’s Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners, formerly Sequoia Capital India & Southeast Asia, Sarvam said Thursday.The Bangalore-based startup, until recently in stealth mode, was co-founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar. It has ambitious plans to build open source foundational AI systems as well as tools for creating apps for the meager compute infrastructure available to developers in India. The startup has a total of 18 employees and is just opening an office in the city."What we are showing is that you can build large language models with limited resources,” Raghavan said in a phone interview. "We are building at a smaller scale and demonstrating that these can be extremely cost and energy efficient so they can be accessed by everyone."Large language models, like OpenAI’s GPT-4 and Meta Platforms Inc.’s Llama, are powerful AI systems that understand by learning from vast amounts of diverse data from the internet and elsewhere to summarize, translate, and create text, audio and video for a wide range of applications. The rivalry to develop ever-more sophisticated models is heating up in Silicon Valley and such efforts have attracted billions of dollars in investments.
Article Summary: Sarvam AI is building large language models targeted at unique uses in Indian languages. The Bangalore-based startup, until recently in stealth mode, was co- founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar. It has ambitious plans to build open source foundational AI systems.

Article Title: ZestMoney set to shut operations this month
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Buy now Pay Later (BNPL) startup ZestMoney has decided to shut operations. The move will impact some 150 employees of the firm, the company's management told employees in a town hall on Tuesday. ZestMoney did not comment. It is learnt that the firm will shut down by the end of this month.The move comes after attempts by the Bengaluru-based startup to get acquired by larger peer PhonePe failed. The deal was called off earlier this year after a due diligence process undertaken by PhonePe, while evaluating the potential acquisition failed to meet its bar. The Walmart-owned fintech major had, however, hired some 130 of ZestMoney's employees.
Article Summary: The move will impact some 150 employees of the firm, the company's management told employees in a town hall on Tuesday. The move comes after attempts by the Bengaluru-based startup to get acquired by larger peer PhonePe failed. The Walmart-owned fintech major had, however, hired some 130 of ZestMoney's employees.

Article Title: Startups will play important role in helping India become 3rd largest economy: CEA Nageswaran
Article Text:
Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran

THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Startups will play an important role in helping India become the third largest economy in the world, Chief Economic Advisor (CEA) to the Union government V Anantha Nageswaran has said.Nageswaran said that tier-2 and 3 cities, including Kerala's capital, have become game-changers in helping startups flourish in the country due to improvements in infrastructure and supportive policies of the government, according to a KSUM release.The CEA, during his Leadership Talk on the concluding day of the Huddle Global 2023 organised by the Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), said that India was the fifth largest economy on course to become the third largest in a few years."In fact, I will say 7-in-7 is the buzz slogan, that is 7 trillion USD economy in seven years. Seven trillion USD economy size by 2030 is possible if India maintains its present growth trajectory, and in that journey startup entrepreneurs are going to play an important role," he is quoted as having said in the release.He was of the view that the active participation of startups in India in developing business models on the foundation of expanding physical and digital infrastructure will continue to generate efficiency, revenue and economic returns for the country."The last decade has seen an exceptional transformation in the startup landscape in India, which has emerged as the third largest ecosystem globally, with over 1.12 lakh startups presently recognised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) across 763 districts."Among them, more than 110 are unicorns with a total valuation of around USD 350 billion," he said.The CEA further said that the country ranks second in innovation quality.He said that innovation in India was not just limited to certain sectors as startups were solving problems in 56 industrial sectors, with 13 per cent of them from IT services, nine per cent from health and life sciences, seven per cent from education, five per cent from agriculture and five per cent from food and beverages.Nageswaran also said it was significant that 49 per cent of the startups were from tier-2 and 3 cities which have turned to be game-changers as the business advantages in these locations enable entrepreneurs to operate at lower costs as compared to tier-1 cities."Apart from improved infrastructure and the government's pro-active policies, the availability of a technically skilled talent pool is a huge advantage for startups to set up and flourish in tier-2 and tier-3 cities," he said.He said that historically there was a perception that small towns were difficult places to conduct business."...but with improved internet penetration, vastly better physical infrastructure, road, rail and air connectivity and supportive government policies, this is no longer true," he said.He also noted Kerala's startup journey has been an inspiring one.The CEA said that KSUM has served as the catalyst since its establishment in 2006 to promote change that propelled the state into the forefront of the global startup arena.KSUM is the Kerala government's nodal agency established in 2006 for entrepreneurship development and incubation activities in the state.Nageswaran said that with over 4,000 registered tech startups, 63 incubators and 10 lakh square feet of incubation space, KSUM has not only met its goal of promoting technology-based entrepreneurship but has also earned the distinguished position of being among the world's top business incubators.The November 16-18 fifth edition of Huddle Global, India's biggest beachside startup conclave, was organised by KSUM at Adimalathura beach, near Vizhinjam, here.Attended by around 1,500 delegates, the event displayed sophisticated products from emerging sectors such as robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, life sciences, space tech, blockchain, IoT, e-governance, fintech, healthtech, agritech, edutech and SaaS from across the country.
Article Summary: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran said tier-2 and 3 cities, including Kerala's capital, have become game-changers in helping startups flourish in the country. CEA said that India was the fifth largest economy on course to become the third largest in a few years.

Article Title: E-Commerce startup Udaan to trim costs ahead of 2025 IPO
Article Text: E-commerce startup Udaan is working to curb costs and forge new partnerships with consumer brands in India as it prepares to go public in 2025.Udaan, which competes with Reliance Industries Ltd. and Walmart Inc.’s Flipkart in helping smaller merchants source their goods, will make an operating profit within 18 months, Chief Executive Officer Vaibhav Gupta said in an interview. That’s set to happen around the same time as its initial public offering, he said.The priority “is steady and predictable financial performance,” Gupta said. “Second, strategically we want to ensure that we are top of mind with shopkeepers, with big manufacturers, and we maintain our relative market share.”Lightspeed Venture Partners-backed Udaan is among startups trying to tap the rapid growth of India’s economy and consumer market, while meeting investor demands for profitability. Udaan, which at its peak employed thousands, joined fellow Indian startups in slashing jobs last year and tightening internal controls and compliance. It now has about 1,800 staff, and Gupta didn’t specify if further job cuts are needed.Corporate governance lapses at Indian online tutoring firm Byju’s, once the country’s top startup with a valuation of $22 billion, shone a light at unique challenges faced by founders in the South Asian nation and drove companies to be more diligent.“We continue to move towards more professionalized management, professionalized board and also institutionalized shareholders as we go towards public markets,” Gupta said.Udaan is yet to decide whether it will list in India or overseas. It was valued at more than $3 billion in a 2021 funding round, and was in talks to raise $400 million, Business Standard reported in September. Lightspeed owns about 35% of Udaan, while Tencent Holdings Ltd. holds 6%.The company was founded in 2016 by three engineers who previously worked at Flipkart. The trio together ran Udaan until Gupta, one of the founders, took over as CEO in 2021. The other two founders — Amod Malviya and Sujeet Kumar — are board members.Udaan built an online marketplace and logistics networks that help mum-and-pop stores get quicker deliveries and cut traditional middlemen out. That kind of digital-led wholesale business still accounts for a very small part of India’s overall retail market but can balloon to $150 billion in sales and yield a 100% return on capital invested in a decade, according to McKinsey & Co. estimates published in the Mint newspaper.Bengaluru-based Udaan has also ventured into financing through its fintech unit which helps shopkeepers get working capital loans to buy inventory. That business is profitable before taxes and is growing 70% annually, Gupta said.“That’s a second business in the overall umbrella of Udaan trying to organize trade in the country,” Gupta said. “In addition to commerce, financing becomes an important market opportunity.”
Article Summary: Udaan will make an operating profit within 18 months, Chief Executive Officer Vaibhav Gupta says. Udaan competes with Reliance Industries Ltd. and Walmart Inc.’s Flipkart in helping smaller merchants source their goods. The priority “is steady and predictable financial performance,” Gupta said.
